`evaluation.run` with `mode: explore` (or inferred explore when narrowing params present) **must** include at least one filter: `grep`, `example_ids`, or `evaluators`. Otherwise the server returns an error — no silent full-suite explore.

- `repetitions` defaults to **1**
- `example_ids` can auto-derive `grep` (OR-joined escaped ids)

**Mode inference (when `mode` omitted):**

- Narrowing params present → explore
- No narrowing → **validate** (CI-safe full suite backward compat)

**How to apply:**

```text
evaluation { action: "run", args: {
  suite_id: "...",
  mode: "explore",
  grep: "patient-zero-smoke"
}}
```

Before merge/ship: `mode: validate` (or omit mode without narrowing for full suite).

**Never:**

- Pass `mode: explore` alone expecting a smoke subset
- Ship on explore pass rate without validate run

name: feedback_factuality_groundedness_split_scoring_artifact
description: Factuality≈0/MAJOR_INACCURACIES + Groundedness passing on the same answers = shared @kbn/evals geometric-mean scoring artifact, not model failure
type: feedback
---

# Factuality/Groundedness Split = Scoring Artifact, Not Model Failure

When a subject model (even Opus) scores near-**0 Factuality** with a uniform
`MAJOR_INACCURACIES` label while the **same answers pass Groundedness**, that is
a **scoring-design artifact** in the shared `@kbn/evals` correctness evaluator —
NOT the subject model being inaccurate. Do not report it as a subject-model
regression on the Security LLM Performance Matrix L3 row.

**Why (root cause, file:line):**
- `x-pack/platform/packages/shared/kbn-evals/src/evaluators/correctness/scoring.ts`
  — `calculateFactualScore` is a **geometric mean** of per-claim scores with
  `CLAIM_FACTUAL_SCORE_MAP`: `NOT_IN_GROUND_TRUTH.central = 0.1`,
  `CONTRADICTED.central = 0.0`. One central claim absent-from or contradicting
  the ground truth collapses the entire Factuality score toward 0.
- `.../correctness/system_prompt.text` — the judge treats the ground truth as
  the *only* valid source (no external knowledge); a central claim not in the
  ground truth → `NOT_IN_GROUND_TRUTH` → summary `MAJOR_INACCURACIES`; a
  functionally-different synonym → `CONTRADICTED` (strict-phrasing rule).
- Interaction: alerts-rag / agent-builder `expected.expected` references are
  deliberately thin / data-agnostic, so a rich, correct, **grounded** answer
  necessarily contains central claims absent from the reference → guaranteed
  ~0 Factuality. Groundedness scores against *retrieved context*, so it passes.

**How to diagnose:** run a per-example failing-score drill and compare the
per-evaluator failing counts. The tell is the split — e.g. build #56 Opus
alerts-rag: **Factuality 90 fails @0** vs **Groundedness 10 fails** on the same
run — plus the Factuality explanation merely echoing the `MAJOR_INACCURACIES`
label (no per-claim rationale). Cross-model + cross-suite uniformity confirms
scoring, not model behavior.

**Fix (shared scorer, needs the pre-merge runtime eval gate — touches every
suite's Factuality):** soften `NOT_IN_GROUND_TRUTH.central` `0.1`→`~0.6`; or
(preferred) exclude `NOT_IN_GROUND_TRUTH` from the Factuality product entirely
("absent from a thin reference" is coverage/relevance, not a factual error).
Tracked: elastic/security-team#18060.

**Never:**
- Report a Factuality/Groundedness split as a subject-model failure.
- Rush a fix into the shared `@kbn/evals` scorer without the runtime eval gate —
  it changes every suite's Factuality.

**Confirmed approach:** live-verified on golden-cluster build #56 (Opus
alerts-rag), 2026-07-05; root cause traced to `scoring.ts` + `system_prompt.text`.

**Related revamp gotcha:** per-example score drills on revamp-era runs must use
the Kibana evals API (getRun → getExperimentScores → normalize), not the legacy
ES read — deployment ES keys 403 on the `.evaluation-scores*` dot-index, so the
legacy path returns "no score documents". `list-runs` shows `scoreCount: 0` for
these runs. Verified: the fallback resolved 1817 scores on the Opus run.

**Zero-cost re-validation lever (added 2026-07-05):** a scorer-map change can be
validated against EXISTING golden verdicts with NO new eval run, because the
`Factuality` evaluator persists the full per-claim `correctnessAnalysis` in its
score `metadata` — see `x-pack/platform/packages/shared/kbn-evals/src/evaluators/correctness/index.ts:157`
(`metadata: { ...(metadata ?? {}), correctnessAnalysis }`), and the qualitative
`Correctness Analysis` evaluator stores `metadata: { ...correctnessAnalysisResult }`
(index.ts:118). So to prove a new `CLAIM_FACTUAL_SCORE_MAP` fixes the artifact:
pull the run's Factuality score docs, extract `metadata.correctnessAnalysis.analysis[]`
(each has `verdict` + `centrality`), and re-run `calculateFactualScore` with old
vs new map. This tests exactly the observed verdicts (the change doesn't touch the
judge, only the number map), so it's a complete validation of the code change —
the only thing it can't show is judge-verdict-distribution shift (which won't
change). Getting the raw docs needs authenticated golden access (evaluationsKbnApiKey);
`evaluation.results` is suite-scoped/limit-100 and not run-scoped, so a direct
`getExperimentScores` call is the cleaner fetch.

**VALIDATED 2026-07-05:** golden creds in `~/.cursor/agent-builder-skill-dev-deployments.json` → `deployments['golden-evals']` (`evaluationsKbnUrl` + `evaluationsKbnApiKey`); two authenticated GETs (headers `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`, `kbn-xsrf:true`, `elastic-api-version:1`): `/internal/evals/experiments?suite_id=&model_id=&page=&per_page=100` (find experiment where `execution_id === <runId>`) then `/internal/evals/experiments/{experiment_id}/scores?suite_id=&execution_id=<runId>` → `{scores:[...]}`; each Factuality doc carries `metadata.correctnessAnalysis.analysis[]`. Re-scoring the softened map across all 6 build-56 alerts-rag models: Factuality failing @0.7 45→4, median 0.224→0.849, Groundedness unchanged 0.984; re-computed OLD median == stored-doc median (sanity ok); the 4 remaining NEW failures were exactly the 4 genuine CONTRADICTED-central examples (all still 0 — fix does not mask real errors). Fed PR elastic/kibana#276331 (now ready-for-review).

# find-security-rules Track B: models route rule-inventory to platform ES|QL, not skill tools

**Type:** feedback
**Domain:** Kibana agent-builder / security-ai-rules evals / matrix C2 L2
**Status:** diagnosis VALIDATED (log-grounded); prose fixes DISPROVEN at THREE levels on golden — skill body, tool descriptions, AND paired negative few-shot (builds #182 + #193, 2026-07-03); framework tool-scoping DOES NOT EXIST — the "real fix" is a cross-team platform capability gap, not a hotfix (2026-07-03, code-grounded)
**Date:** 2026-07-02 (updated 2026-07-03, twice)

## The finding (validated)

On the Security LLM matrix, **C2 (Detection Engineering) L2 (Tool Trajectory) = 0.0
across ALL 6 models** — a hard zero, not partial. This is *not* a wiring, golden-ID,
or skill-registration bug (all ruled out with code evidence):

- Trajectory evaluator LCS/coverage math is correct.
- Goldens `[security.discover_rule_tags, security.find_rules]` match the registered
  tool IDs exactly (`find_rules_tool.ts`, `discover_rule_tags_tool.ts`).
- `dexAiSkillFindRules` flag is enabled in the `evals_security_ai_rules` Scout config
  and was already present at the build being analyzed (commit `18b6e7ce`).
- L1 Skill Invoked (find-security-rules) = 1 → the SKILL.md **is loaded**.

**Root cause:** on find-rules routing examples the agent loads the
`find-security-rules` skill (reads SKILL.md) but then calls
`platform.core.generate_esql` / `execute_esql` against `.siem-signals-default`
(the *alerts* index) instead of `security.find_rules` / `security.discover_rule_tags`.
Two independent evaluators agree: `ToolUsageOnly=0` AND `Trajectory=0` for the 3
find-rules examples (the aggregate `ToolUsageOnly=0.63` is the 5 non-find examples
auto-passing, 5/8=0.625 — a decoy, not partial success).

**Evidence:** weekly build #51, security-ai-rules / eis-anthropic-claude-4-6-opus,
trace `a7c9d8300f28787e0c531749b8e4c777`, verbatim:
```
FROM .siem-signals-default
| WHERE kibana.alert.rule.threat.technique.id == "T1059"
| STATS rule_names = VALUES(kibana.alert.rule.name)
```
(via `@kbn/agent-builder-genai-utils/tools/generate_esql/graph.js`). Uniform across
all 6 EIS models → a model-prior problem ("data question ⇒ ES|QL"), not a per-model
capability gap.

## Why the matrix was right

The C2 L2=0 cell is an **honest signal**, not a matrix defect — it correctly surfaces
that current frontier models mis-route rule-inventory NL queries. Do NOT "fix" it by
marking the trajectory N/A or gaming the score; that would fabricate a pass. Every
other N/A cell in the matrix is intentional/documented (C5 excluded, C6 by-design
NA, C7 deferred, L5 observability-only).

## The lever (key lesson)

SKILL.md **body** prose is loaded *after* skill selection and does not compete at
tool-selection time. When the model picks a tool, it ranks **tool descriptions** —
and `platform.core.generate_esql`'s broad description sits right next to
`security.find_rules`. So the effective lever for tool routing is the **inline tool
`description` fields**, not more SKILL.md body prose (which was already maxed:
skill description, SKILL.md, and both tool descriptions all said "never ES|QL").

**Fix applied (fix/weekly-evals-matrix):** moved intent-ownership + the anti-ES|QL
directive into the tool descriptions themselves:
- `find_rules` description now leads with "THE tool for listing/counting/filtering
  rules — rules covering T1059, rules tagged with MITRE, …; detection rules are
  managed saved objects NOT indexed documents; do NOT use generate_esql/execute_esql
  — ES|QL over .alerts/.siem-signals returns fired alerts, never rule definitions."
- `discover_rule_tags` description now leads with "First step for ANY rule-inventory
  question … never reach for generate_esql/execute_esql to inventory rules."

## Caveat / escalation path

Efficacy is uncertain — a model with a strong "data ⇒ ES|QL" prior may ignore tool
descriptions too. If descriptions don't move all models, escalate to the structural
fix: **scope out platform ES|QL tools when the find-security-rules skill is active**
(agent-builder framework tool-scoping) rather than relying on prose. Prose/description
is the cheap first attempt; tool-scoping is the durable fix.

## Local-Scout validation is blocked by a CCM connector circular-dep (do NOT rabbit-hole)

Attempting `run-local-matrix-suite.sh smoke security-ai-rules routing-find-mitre-tag`
to validate the fix hit a genuine infra circular dependency (cost ~40 min, no signal):

1. `node scripts/eis` provisions the EIS `.inference` **chat_completion endpoints**
   in ES (via CCM). Good — models are usable.
2. The eval's `createConnectorFixture` (SKIP unset) tries to **create** a `.inference`
   *action connector*, which tries to **create the inference endpoint** →
   `500 "Inference with id .anthropic-…-chat_completion … already exists"`. Conflict.
3. Setting `KBN_EVALS_SKIP_CONNECTOR_SETUP=true` (skip create, use preconfigured) does
   NOT help: `KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS` is read by the **Playwright eval config**,
   NOT injected into the running Kibana as preconfigured connectors —
   `GET /api/actions/connectors` still lists **0** `.inference` connectors.
4. `scout.js start-server` **wipes ES on every (re)start** (fresh cluster; no
   `--preserveEsData` for stateful classic), so restarting to "bake" connectors
   destroys the EIS endpoints AND the CCM key you just provisioned → preconfigured
   connectors reference dead endpoints.

Net: create-path conflicts with pre-provisioned endpoints; skip-path has no
preconfigured connectors; restart wipes provisioning. `run-local-matrix-suite.sh`'s
`stack-boot` claims to resolve this (build-from-ES → restart-with-env baked), but its
success gate `probe_preconfigured_connector` presumes Scout registers
`KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS` as preconfigured, which was NOT observed here (count 0).
Also `stack-boot`'s first-pass 180s wait is too short for a cold from-source boot, so
it bails before ever running EIS.

**Reliable validation path instead:** on-demand CI (`kibana-evals-on-demand-llm-evals`,
security-ai-rules, Sonnet subject) on the pushed branch, or the next weekly — CI
provisions connectors cleanly. Fix committed `fix/weekly-evals-matrix` @ `557a50c97abc`
(tool-description edits, 60 unit tests green). Empirical routing signal (does Sonnet
now call `security.find_rules`?) still PENDING that CI run. Before spending time on
local Scout for EIS-model routing evals, resolve the preconfigured-connector question
first (does `stack-boot` actually register them? what format?) — otherwise it is a
40-min dead end.

## VALIDATION RESULT (2026-07-03): tool-description fix DISPROVEN

On-demand build **#182** (`kibana-evals-on-demand-llm-evals`, security-ai-rules,
subject `eis-anthropic-claude-4.6-sonnet`, commit `557a50c`) **passed** (green build)
— but the build passing is NOT the score. Reading the golden `.evaluation-scores*`
datastream + OTLP traces proves the fix did **not** work:

- find-rules routing examples (ex 3,4,5 of `rule-generation-routing`):
  `Trajectory` label=`poor`, **LCS 0/2, coverage 0/2** — Sonnet matched neither
  `security.discover_rule_tags` nor `security.find_rules`. `ToolUsageOnly=0`.
- Golden routing trace (ex 3 "List all enabled detection rules tagged with MITRE",
  trace `a4f4e3327beb7c869e52ec823b0219bd`): 418 steps, 613K input tokens, 412s.
  Tool calls: `load_skill` ×2 → `platform.core.search` → `natural_language_search`
  → `platform.core.list_indices` ×4 → **`platform.core.generate_esql` ×2** →
  **`platform.core.execute_esql` ×7 retries** → `get_index_mapping`. NEVER called
  `security.find_rules` / `security.discover_rule_tags`.

So strengthening the two tool `description` fields (557a50c) did NOT change Sonnet's
"data question ⇒ ES|QL" prior. The cheap lever is exhausted; the **framework
tool-scoping** fix (scope out `platform.core.generate_esql`/`execute_esql` when the
find-security-rules skill is active) is now the required path, not optional.

**Two verification gotchas surfaced (both cost-savers next time):**
1. **A green on-demand build ≠ recovered score.** The trajectory is not
   hard-gating, so the build passes while C2 L2 stays 0. Always read the actual
   golden score/trace, not the build status. (verify-bug-fix-claims-before-pr)
2. **`.evaluation-scores*` coerces N/A(null)→score 0.** Naive `mean(score)` over the
   8 routing examples reads 0.0 but 5/8 are `label:"N/A"` (rule-creation ex 0,1,2 +
   distractors ex 6,7). The REAL signal is the 3 find-rules examples
   (`label:"poor"`). **Filter `label==='N/A'` before averaging** any trajectory
   cell — the raw mean is polluted. (Matrix aggregation must exclude label=N/A too.)

**Do NOT trigger the weekly on 557a50c** — it would re-report C2 L2=0. Fix
tool-scoping first, re-run on-demand Sonnet, confirm find-rules trace calls
`security.find_rules`, THEN weekly.

## VALIDATION RESULT #2 (2026-07-03): paired negative few-shot ALSO DISPROVEN — prose door CLOSED

The one prose lever not yet tried was a **paired WRONG→RIGHT negative few-shot**
in the SKILL.md body (❌ "List rules tagged MITRE" → generate_esql/execute_esql;
✅ → discover_rule_tags → find_rules). Added as a "Routing (read first)" section
in `find_rules_skill.ts`, committed `3bc9f3efc464`, pushed `upstream/fix/weekly-evals-matrix`,
on-demand build **#193** (security-ai-rules, subject `eis-anthropic-claude-4.6-sonnet`)
— **passed** (green), but the golden score is UNCHANGED:

- run `bk-019f274a-63af-4b5d-98bd-25201d32ecd0::anthropic-claude-4.6-sonnet`,
  `security-ai-rules: rule-generation-routing`. The 3 find-rules **inventory**
  examples ("How many custom rules are enabled?", "List all enabled rules tagged
  with MITRE", "Show me rules covering T1059") all `Trajectory` label=`poor`,
  **LCS 0/2, coverage 0/2**. Verbatim evaluator explanation:
  `Missing tools: security.discover_rule_tags, security.find_rules. Extra tools:
  load_skill ×2, platform.core.search, platform.core.list_indices, platform.core.generate_esql,
  platform.core.execute_esql ×7 …`
- The other 5 examples are correctly N/A: 3 rule-creation ("Alert when…",
  "Detect suspicious access…") scored via ExpectedToolCalled/ForbiddenToolNotCalled,
  2 distractors (dashboards, APM) no-annotation. Confirms the N/A-pollution
  lesson from result #1.

So prose hardening is now falsified at **all three levels**: (1) SKILL.md body
prohibitions, (2) tool `description` fields, (3) paired negative few-shot. Sonnet's
"data question ⇒ ES|QL" prior overrides every prose signal because
`platform.core.generate_esql` stays bound and competitive at selection time the
whole round. **The framework tool-scoping fix (Option A) is the only remaining path.**
Decision to escalate is the operator's; do not spend further cycles on skill-body prose.

Gotcha reinforced: **ForbiddenToolNotCalled=1.0 is a decoy for the inventory examples**
— its forbidden set is `security.create_detection_rule` (don't create when asked to
list), NOT the ES|QL tools. Only the `Trajectory` evaluator's coverage/extra-tools
list exposes the ES|QL misroute. Read the trajectory explanation, not the aggregate.

## General rule

For agent-builder skill routing misses where the skill LOADS (L1=1) but the wrong
tools are called: the fix lives in **tool descriptions** (selection-time context),
not SKILL.md body. If that fails, the durable fix is framework tool-scoping, not more
prose. Diagnose with `ToolUsageOnly` + `Trajectory` agreement and the OTLP trace's
actual tool spans — never infer from the aggregate mean (non-annotated examples
auto-pass and inflate it).

## FRAMEWORK VERDICT (2026-07-03, code-grounded): per-skill tool exclusion is NOT supported

Investigated the Agent Builder framework in `~/Projects/kibana` before attempting the
"scope out platform ES|QL" fix. **The framework cannot subtract tools when a skill is
active.** Tool selection is allowlist-only / additive:

- `SkillDefinition` (`x-pack/platform/packages/shared/agent-builder/agent-builder-server/skills/type_definition.ts:61-122`)
  exposes only `getRegistryTools` / `getInlineTools` — **additive**. No
  `exclude_tool_ids`, `denied_tools`, or tool-filter field. Persisted skills use
  `tool_ids` (max 5) the same additive way (`agent-builder-common/skills/validation.ts:82-105`).
- `selectTools` (`agent_builder/server/services/execution/run_agent/utils/select_tools.ts:78-95`)
  binds `defaultAgentToolIds` whenever `enable_elastic_capabilities: true` (default agent).
  `defaultAgentToolIds` (`agent-builder-common/tools/constants.ts:111-124`) **includes**
  `platform.core.generate_esql` + `platform.core.execute_esql`. Selection is

name: feedback_gh_update_branch_workflow_scope_403
description: gh update-branch on a stale fork PR 403s without `workflow` token scope; rebase+force-push sidesteps it
type: feedback
---

# Updating a stale fork PR branch: the `workflow` OAuth scope trap

`gh api --method PUT repos/elastic/kibana/pulls/<N>/update-branch` (and any HTTPS push that
carries changes to `.github/workflows/*.yml`) **fails with HTTP 403** when the token lacks the
`workflow` scope:

```
refusing to allow an OAuth App to create or update workflow
`.github/workflows/backlog-groom.lock.yml` without `workflow` scope
```

**Why:** GitHub blocks any push/merge that *modifies workflow files* unless the token has
`workflow` scope. When a fork PR branch is far behind `main` (Kibana drifts ~66 commits/day, so a
~2–3 week-old base is 1000+ behind), the "update branch" merge pulls in upstream `.github/workflows`
changes → the merge commit touches workflow files → 403. The default `gh` login scope set
(`repo, read:org, gist, read:packages, read:project`) does **not** include `workflow`.

**How to apply — three ways to clear `prbot:outdated` on a stale fork PR:**
1. **Rebase our own commits onto fresh `main` + force-push** (preferred, no scope change). Our
   commits don't touch workflow files, so the *pushed* commits carry no workflow diff → no 403.
   Needs a force-push to the **fork feature branch** (safe; never to `main`/`master`). Re-runs
   `kibana-ci` (~60 min). Get explicit go-ahead before force-pushing.
2. `gh auth refresh -s workflow` (interactive) then re-run the `update-branch` API — keeps history,
   adds a merge commit.
3. Defer until right before merge — `prbot:outdated` is **advisory** and re-stales as `main` moves,
   so updating early on a review-blocked PR just wastes a CI cycle.

**Never:**
- Assume `update-branch` will "just work" on a long-lived fork PR — check `behind_by` first.
- Force-push without explicit user approval, even to a feature branch.
- Force-push to `main`/`master`.

**Confirmed approach:** Hit the 403 on `elastic/kibana#276310` (branch 1185 behind `main`); token
had only `repo` scope. Verified the rebase-and-force-push path avoids it because our 2 commits
never touched `.github/workflows`.

# Golden Serverless Golden Cluster — No Evaluations UI App

`kbn-evals-serverless-ed035a` ingests scores and serves **`/internal/evals/*`** (with proper API headers) but does **not** register the Evaluations Kibana nav app. Deep links to `/app/evals/experiments/...` show **"Application not found"** even when experiment metadata resolves correctly.

**Why:** Confirmed Jun 26 2026 when matrix HTML linked `f2d426e779923e90::anthropic-claude-4.5-haiku` to `/app/evals/experiments/...`. Internal API returned experiments with `EvaluationsKbnClient` headers; browser UI route failed. Scores live in Discover (`kibana-evaluations*`, `.evaluation-scores*`).

**How to apply:**
- Treat **`evaluationsUiAvailable: false`** for `kbn-evals-serverless-*` hostnames (override with `EVALUATIONS_UI_AVAILABLE=1` if UI ships later).
- Matrix / tooling deep links: use **Discover filtered by** `metadata.execution_id`, `run_id`, or `execution_id.keyword` — not `/app/evals/experiments/...`.
- Keep **agent MCP probes** (`evaluation.failing-examples`, `diagnose.explain-failures`) — they use API/MCP, not the UI.
- `EvaluationsKbnClient` probes need headers: `x-elastic-internal-origin: agent-builder-skill-dev`, `elastic-agent-builder-version: 1`, `kbn-xsrf: true`. Raw `fetch` without them can falsely suggest API is disabled.

**Never:**
- Assume `/internal/evals/experiments` 400 without client headers means no data on cluster.
- Emit Evaluations / Tracing header links on serverless golden cluster without UI availability check.

**Confirmed approach:** API probe via dist client returned experiments; UI screenshot "Application not found"; fix landed in skill-dev `matrix_golden_links.ts` (Discover run URLs + warning).

# Golden per-example retrieval: action selection (agent-builder eval suite)

**Context:** Drilling per-example skill-activation scores from the golden
cluster (`kbn-evals-serverless-ed035a`) for the Security LLM matrix.

## What works / what's lossy (verified 2026-07-05, build `bk-019f2c05`)

The golden `evaluationsKbnApiKey` **works** — the limitation is *which MCP
action* you call, not auth or ingest:

- **`evaluation.results { suite_id }`** — returns the FULL per-example score set
  (e.g. 1817 rows) but is **single-run-by-design** ("most recent results for a
  suite"). It does **not** support `run_id`/model selection — passing a run_id
  is ignored and you still get the most-recent run. So it gives one model fully
  (whichever ran most recently), not all models.
- **`evaluation.compare-models { suite_id: "agent-builder" }`** — returns empty
  / 1-model garbage (token evaluators averaged into meanScore) for this suite.
- **`evaluation.failing-examples { run_id }`** — accepts run_id but returns only
  a small FAILING subset (~16 rows for Opus, data-exploration-dominated); passing
  examples are absent, so you cannot see activation rates for skills that passed.

**Consequence:** there is currently **no clean per-model per-example retrieval**
for the agent-builder suite. Use `evaluation.results` for the single most-recent
run's complete data; per-model drill needs a plugin fix (add run_id/model
selector to `results`, or fix `compare-models`).

## Vault / MCP hydration

- `deployment.ensure-golden-evals` runs `vault read` in the **MCP process env**.
  If the MCP has `VAULT_ADDR` unset it hits `https://127.0.0.1:8200` (local vault,
  usually down) and **skips hydration** even after you `vault login` in a shell.
- Durable fix: `launchctl setenv VAULT_ADDR https://secrets.elastic.co:8200`
  (takes effect for MCP on next Cursor relaunch). Corporate vault needs
  `VAULT_ADDR=https://secrets.elastic.co:8200 vault login --method oidc` first.
- The stored key can still be fully functional (reads `.evaluation-scores`) even
  when `ensure-golden-evals` reports "hydration skipped" — check `evaluation.results`
  before assuming the key is broken.

## Reusable parse

`evaluation.results` payload shape: `{ runs:[{id,modelId,branch,...}],
scores:[{runId,exampleIndex,input,evaluatorName,score,passed,datasetName,traceId}] }`.
Join scores→runs by `runId`; filter `evaluatorName` starts-with `Skill Invoked (`
and group by `(datasetName, exampleIndex)` to see which skill fired per example.
`fired=(none)` on a happy-path example = the agent used a raw tool (e.g. ES|QL)
without activating any skill — the classic ES|QL-collision signature.

name: feedback_grep_count_single_line_html
description: Grep count-mode returns matched LINES not occurrences — build-injected single-line HTML shows "1" even with many hits; don't read it as "content missing"
type: feedback
---

# Grep count-mode on build-injected single-line HTML

`Grep` with `output_mode:"count"` reports **matched lines, not matched
occurrences**. When a build step injects an entire rendered markdown doc as a
**single minified line** of HTML (or JSON-encodes it into one JS string), every
match on that doc collapses onto one line — so `count` returns `1` no matter how
many times the string actually appears, and a multi-pattern alternation returns
`1` total. This looks exactly like "my content didn't land" when it did.

**Why:** Observed 2026-07-04 verifying `alignment-board.html`
(`scripts/build-board.mjs` injects 14 docs). After adding a "LOC budget"
section and a "registerActionProvider" note, a combined `count` grep returned
`1`; a second combined grep returned `1`; only per-pattern greps confirmed both
were present. Wasted two round-trips chasing a phantom regression.

**How to apply:**
- To confirm build-injected content is present, prefer **`output_mode:"content"`
  with a narrow, unique substring** (returns the matching line so you see it) or
  grep the **source markdown** the build reads, not the minified output.
- If you must use `count`, run **one pattern per call** and remember the number
  is *lines*, not *hits*; on single-line HTML the ceiling is effectively `1`.
- Faster still: trust the build log (`✓ Injected N docs (KB)`) + a
  content-mode spot check on one unique phrase, rather than counting.

**Never:**
- Conclude "content missing / regression" from a `count` of `1` on
  build-injected HTML.
- Use a multi-pattern alternation in `count` mode and infer per-pattern
  presence from the total.

**Confirmed approach:** Per-pattern content-mode greps resolved the false
alarm; the sections were present the whole time.

name: feedback_headless_colima_cell_reboot_survival
description: Two colima/docker gotchas that silently break unattended reboot survival of an EDD cell — restart=unless-stopped does NOT revive an explicitly-stopped container, and colima must have exactly ONE owner
type: feedback
confidence: strong
updated: 2026-07-03
source: m1max headless EDD runner setup (Jul 3 2026) — both bugs hit live while wiring reboot survival; validated fixes
---

# Headless colima EDD-cell reboot survival — two silent traps

Wiring an EDD dev cell (ES + EDOT collector + Kibana) to survive an unattended reboot on a
headless macOS box, two non-obvious things will silently break recovery. Both bit the m1max
setup live. Applies to any colima-based cell (i9 / M4 / m1max), not just Apple Silicon.

## Trap 1 — `restart=unless-stopped` does NOT revive an *explicitly stopped* container

Docker's `unless-stopped` policy restarts a container when it **crashes** or when the docker
daemon restarts (reboot) **and the container was running at shutdown**. It deliberately does
**NOT** restart a container that was **explicitly `docker stop`'d**. That's a problem for the
**EDOT collector** (`kibana-edot-collector`): it's created/managed by a helper process
(Kibana's EDOT plugin / `scripts/edot_collector.js`), and when *that* process shuts down it
issues a clean `docker stop` on the container. So after the manager exits (or Kibana
restarts), the EDOT container sits in `Exited (0)` and `unless-stopped` will **never** bring
it back on its own — and because it wasn't running at shutdown, a reboot won't either.
Symptom: Kibana serves 200 but `docker ps` shows only ES; `traces-*` stays empty; Kibana logs
`ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:4318`.

**Fix:** the launchd Kibana supervisor must **explicitly `docker start` the cell containers**
on every launch — don't rely on the restart policy alone. Idempotent guard:
```bash
for c in es-edd-runner kibana-edot-collector; do
  [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$c" 2>/dev/null)" = "false" ] \
    && docker start "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1
done
```
Keep `restart=unless-stopped` on them too (covers crash + daemon-restart cases). Do NOT write
a supervisor comment like "ES + EDOT come back on their own (restart=unless-stopped)" — that
assumption is the bug.

## Trap 2 — colima must have exactly ONE owner

Running colima via **two** mechanisms at once — a manual `colima start` **and**
`brew services start colima` (a launchd job) — makes them fight over the same
`~/.colima/default` VM. The brew service errored, **tore down the running cell containers**,
and left the **docker daemon socket unreachable while `colima status` still reported
"running"** (colima status checks the VM, not the in-VM dockerd). Symptom: `docker ps` →
"Cannot connect to the Docker daemon at .../docker.sock", ES/Kibana die, but `colima status`
looks fine and misleads you.

**Fix / decision:** pick a single owner. For an EDD cell, let the **launchd Kibana supervisor
own colima** (`colima status >/dev/null 2>&1 || colima start ...`) — do NOT also register
`brew services start colima`. Recovery when already wedged: `colima stop && colima start`
(clean), then **probe `docker ps` a few times** to confirm the daemon is actually stable
before rebuilding — a single probe can pass right before the daemon drops again.

## Confirmed reboot-survival chain (what actually works)
autologin (kcpassword) → launchd agent `RunAtLoad` → supervisor `colima start` → supervisor
`docker start` ES+EDOT (Trap 1 fix) → wait ES health → start Kibana; containers also carry
`restart=unless-stopped` as a backstop. Cross-refs: `reference_m1max_apple_silicon_runner`,
`reference_headless_macos_runner_setup`, `feedback_persistent_daemons_via_launchd_runatload`,
`feedback_edot_capsule_trace_tls_drop`.

name: feedback_headroom_system_message_compression_unsafe
description: HEADROOM_COMPRESS_SYSTEM_MESSAGES=1 hangs the whole proxy under chatty clients (Claude Code) — single-concurrency ONNX backend serializes large system prompts
type: feedback
confidence: proven
---

# Headroom `HEADROOM_COMPRESS_SYSTEM_MESSAGES=1` Is Unsafe As-Is

Headroom (`:8788`) system-prompt compression serializes through a single-concurrency ONNX
Kompress backend (intentional — avoids CPU thrash). For a chatty client like Claude Code,
concurrent large system-message requests queue behind each other, and individual
compressions can take **8-9+ minutes**, hanging the whole proxy (`/readyz`/`/stats` time
out, CPU pinned).

**If this happens:** revert immediately — unset `HEADROOM_COMPRESS_SYSTEM_MESSAGES` and
restart. Don't re-enable without also raising `HEADROOM_KOMPRESS_MAX_CONCURRENT` or
exempting large system prompts from the ONNX path.

**Separate gotcha:** a leftover orphaned "persistent-task" Headroom deployment profile from
an unrelated skill-dev session can silently race the real `claude` LaunchAgent for port
`8788` after any restart. Run `headroom install remove` to permanently remove it — don't
just kill the process, or it respawns and re-races the port.

name: feedback_heredoc_stdin_collision
description: python3 heredoc-as-script reads stdin for the program, so a piped data feed is swallowed; passes bash -n + shellcheck, only running catches it — pass data via env var
type: feedback
---

# Heredoc-as-script Collides With Piped stdin

`python3 - <<'PY' … PY` tells Python to read its **program** from stdin (the
`-`). If you then pipe data into that command (`producer | python3 - <<'PY'`),
`sys.stdin.read()` does **not** get the piped data — the heredoc already *is*
stdin. The pipe is silently swallowed; the parser sees empty/garbage input.

**Why:** Hit in a converse-smoke script — `converse | analyze` where `analyze`
ran `python3 - <<'PY'` and expected the converse JSON on stdin. It never
arrived. `bash -n` and `shellcheck -S warning` both passed the file clean (it's
valid syntax, wrong semantics) — only *running* it against a fixture surfaced
the `JSONDecodeError`.

**How to apply:** When a shell function must run an embedded Python program
**and** consume data, decouple program from data:
- Pass data via an environment variable: `RAW="$json" python3 <<'PY'` then
  `os.environ['RAW']`. Env vars carry arbitrary quotes/newlines safely.
- Or write the program to a temp `.py` file and `python3 that.py < data`.
- Never combine `python3 - <<'HEREDOC'` (script from stdin) with a stdin data
  feed.

**Never:**
- Trust `bash -n` / `shellcheck` to catch this — it's a clean-passing semantic
  bug. Behaviorally test with a real fixture.

**Confirmed approach:** Env-var passing fixed it; re-tested 4/4 fixtures
(happy, filestore.read variant, distractor, non-JSON 500) all correct.

name: feedback_hermes_wrapper_model_alias_dropped
description: hermes-wrapper.py silently dropped literal (non-alias) model ids, so treadmill task-execution never actually ran ornith despite config saying so
type: feedback
confidence: proven
updated: 2026-07-07
source: Daybreak S0 spike setup, ornith-on-i9 verification (Jul 6-7 2026)
---

# hermes-wrapper.py silently dropped literal model ids (ornith never actually ran)

## Symptom
Treadmill's `ao-config.yaml` routes `task-execution` → `ornith-lmstudio`
(`cliModel: ornith-1.0-35b-mtplx`, `cliProvider: lm-studio`), and the fleet
preamble/dispatch looked correctly wired end-to-end. But nothing about the
actual model used was ever verified live — until a dedicated smoke test
proved the wrapper was quietly not doing what the config said.

## Root cause
`hermes-wrapper.py` runs `_resolve_model_alias(model)` on any `-m` value that
doesn't contain a `/` (its heuristic for "this must be a known short alias
like `sonnet`, not a literal id"). `ornith-1.0-35b-mtplx` is a literal LM
Studio model id, not a known alias, so `MODEL_ALIASES.get()` returned `None`.
The wrapper then set `resolved_model = ""` and **omitted `-m` entirely** from
the `hermes chat` invocation — Hermes silently fell back to its own default
model (GitHub Copilot Claude via the local `:20128` proxy) instead of ornith.

**Net effect: treadmill's `task-execution` route had almost certainly never
actually run ornith, despite `ao-config.yaml` saying it should.** No error was
raised anywhere in the chain; the job "succeeded," just on the wrong model.

## Fix
Fall back to the raw/unresolved model string when alias resolution fails,
instead of dropping it — pass literal ids through verbatim and let Hermes
itself validate/reject.

## Verification
Re-shipped wrapper to the i9, ran the *exact* command treadmill dispatches:
stderr showed `Model 'ornith-1.0-35b-mtplx' ... passing through verbatim`
and the result event was `subtype: success` with a real `PONG` reply from
ornith on the M1 Max (~33s round trip, cold 35B MoE first-token latency).

## Related, distinct gotcha found during the same investigation
Stale/orphaned `hermes` / `hermes-wrapper.py` / `typescript-language-server`
processes left behind by earlier failed or timed-out dispatch attempts on a
fleet node compete for the single LM Studio inference slot and RAM, causing
**new** dispatches to hang or exit non-zero almost instantly. This looks like
a wrapper or model-ID bug but is actually resource contention from process
pileup — kill the stale PIDs on the node first, and prefer adding pre-dispatch
cleanup of orphaned hermes processes to `fleet-manager.ts` over re-diagnosing
the wrapper each time this recurs.

## Never
- Assume a fleet route "must be running the configured model" just because
  dispatch succeeds and no error surfaces — silently-wrong-model failures
  don't throw; verify with a smoke test that greps the actual model id out
  of wrapper stderr/stream output.

name: feedback_host_saturation_kills_orbstack
description: Orbstack crashes under high host memory pressure (load avg >30, 0GB free); before debugging a "flaky" daemon, check host load and free any non-essential dev servers
type: feedback
confidence: strong
updated: 2026-07-01
source: elastic-llm-benchmarker session — daemon died 4+ times with cryptic ConnectionError to ES; root cause was Orbstack OOM-killed under load avg 32
---

# Host Saturation Kills Orbstack (Not Your Daemon)

When a daemon that depends on local ES/Docker dies with a `ConnectionError` to `localhost:9223`, **do not immediately blame the daemon's error handling**. First check `uptime` and `vm_stat`. Orbstack (and Docker Desktop on Mac) can be OOM-killed by the OS under memory pressure, which presents to the daemon as a transient ES outage — and any in-flight write fails.

## Failure mode observed

```
load averages: 37.62 30.01 34.04
free: 0.00 GB

→ Orbstack killed → docker.sock unreachable
→ benchmarker daemon's ES write throws ConnectionError
→ daemon can't persist Stage 1 results
→ queue entry marked failed
→ daemon exits
```

Three crashes in 30 minutes, each right after Stage 1 benchmarks finished (the moment results need to be written to ES). The log showed the error as `error_message: ""` because `ConnectionError.message` was empty — looked like a daemon bug, was actually the host dying.

## Correct pattern

1. **Always check `uptime` first** when a daemon dies with a network/ES error. Load avg >20 on a laptop = saturation territory.
2. **Free dev resources before debugging daemon resilience**. Kibana dev servers are the biggest controllable consumers (~1.5-3 GB each). One `pkill -f "kibana.*--dev"` dropped load from 37 → 4.94 in this session.
3. **Restart Orbstack explicitly** after freeing memory: `open -a OrbStack && sleep 15 && docker ps`.
4. **Verify ES health before re-launching daemon**: `curl http://localhost:9223/_cluster/health`.

## Triage checklist

| Symptom | Likely cause | Check |
|---|---|---|
| Daemon ConnectionError to ES | Orbstack down | `docker ps` — if `daemon not running`, Orbstack is dead |
| Orbstack repeatedly dies | Host memory pressure | `uptime` — load avg >20 |
| Daemon dies silently mid-run | ES write failed in catch block | grep daemon log for `ConnectionError` or `error_message: ""` |
| Stage 1 passes, Stage 2 fails on store | ES killed right after benchmark done | Check timestamps — ES usually dies under load during the write, not the benchmark |

## Never

- Assume a daemon bug when the host is at load avg 30+.
- Restart Orbstack without freeing host memory first — it will crash again immediately.
- Run the benchmarker daemon alongside active Kibana dev servers on a laptop — both compete for the same RAM pool.
- Trust an empty `error_message` field in a failed queue entry — the actual error is in the stack trace below it.

## Confirmed approach

Jul 1, 2026: benchmarker daemon crashed 4 times in 30 min with ES `ConnectionError`. Root cause was Orbstack OOM-killed under load avg 32 (active Kibana dev servers + Cursor + Elastic Endpoint agent). Stopping 2 Kibana dev servers dropped load to 4.46; Orbstack stayed up; daemon completed Stage 1 cleanly on next run.

description: "Kibana security_solution Jest workers are ~500MB-1GB each; default (cores-1) spawn count saturates host RAM. Always cap with --maxWorkers=4 --workerIdleMemoryLimit=512MB at the CLI, never edit committed jest.config"
type: feedback
confidence: strong

source: "empty-window session — a single `node scripts/jest` run in security_solution spawned 15 jest-worker children (~985MB peak each), ~11GB total, load avg 43, 138MB free RAM"
---

# Cap Jest Workers to Avoid Host RAM Exhaustion

Jest defaults to `(CPU cores - 1)` worker processes. On this 16-core machine that spawns ~15 `jest-worker/build/workers/processChild.js` children. In Kibana's `x-pack/solutions/security/plugins/security_solution` suite each worker grows to **~500MB-1GB RSS**, so a single test run consumes **~11GB** and can drive the host to load avg 40+ with near-zero free RAM (thrashing the compressor + swap).

**Always** run Jest with an explicit cap:

```bash
node scripts/jest --config <config> --maxWorkers=4 --workerIdleMemoryLimit=512MB <path>
```

- `--maxWorkers=4` — hard cap on worker processes (also `-w 4`; `--maxWorkers=50%` is portable but ~8 on this box, still heavy).
- `--workerIdleMemoryLimit=512MB` — restarts a worker once it exceeds the limit, stopping the slow RSS creep (workers were seen ballooning from ~470MB to ~985MB over a run).
- For a single narrow test path, `--runInBand` (`-i`) is the lowest-RAM alternative.

**Why:** This connects to `feedback_host_saturation_kills_orbstack` — load avg >20 on a laptop OOM-kills Orbstack and makes dependent daemons/ES throw cryptic ConnectionErrors. Uncapped Jest is a top controllable cause of that saturation.

## How to apply

- Append the flags at the CLI at runtime. This is enforced for the agent via the personal Cursor user rule "Always cap Jest workers to limit RAM" (created 2026-07-02 via `cursor_dialog` item=rule scope=user; lives in `~/.cursor`, so it is never committed).
- For the user's own manual terminal runs, a `~/.zshrc` function/alias is the personal-only equivalent (agent user rules don't affect manual shells).

## Never

- **Never** edit committed Jest config (`jest.config.js` / `jest.config.dev.js`) to enforce a personal worker cap — that change would be pushed to the repo and affect everyone. Keep the cap at the CLI / user-rule layer.
- Never launch a full-parallel Kibana Jest run alongside active Kibana dev servers + Orbstack on a laptop — combined RAM pressure saturates the host.

## Confirmed approach

Jul 2, 2026: diagnosed 47G used / 138MB free / 23G compressor / load avg 43. Top 16 processes were one Jest run's workers (~11GB). Established the `--maxWorkers=4 --workerIdleMemoryLimit=512MB` cap and codified it as an always-on personal user rule rather than a repo-committed config change — a direct instance of `feedback_make_sure_means_automation` ("make sure to X whenever Y" = create a rule/hook/skill).

# `kbn-evals` Evaluator Placement Pattern

Two related, operator-stated conventions for where evaluator code lives.

## Never edit `@kbn/evals` core to fix a single suite

If an evaluator, system prompt, or scoring logic in the shared `@kbn/evals`
package needs a change for one suite's sake, **copy the original logic into
that suite and modify the copy there** — don't edit the shared package
directly. The shared package affects every suite's scores, so a shared change
needs the full validation path (draft PR + on-demand-from-commit eval gate),
not a same-PR side-fix; see `feedback_shared_kbn_evals_change_validation.md`.

## New domain-specific evaluators go outside core

When adding a new evaluator for a specific domain (e.g. security), it should
**live outside the main `kbn-evals` package** — check for an existing
sibling/extension package pattern (e.g. a `kbn-evals-extensions`-style
package, or whatever pattern other teams already used for a similar case)
before adding it to core. Prefer a shared/common package scoped to the domain
(e.g. security) that multiple suites can depend on, over bloating the
generic `kbn-evals` package.

**Confirmed approach:** operator correction, 2026-07-07 (weekly-evals-matrix
worktree session) — "new evaluator should live outside of main kbn-evals
package, use kbn-evals-extensions or check what is the pattern others took in
similar case? you can always create shared/common package for security".

# Golden-cluster traces are mandatory PR evidence for Agent Builder platform tools

## Operator correction (2026-07-13)

After a local `find_rules.spec.ts` run passed on Sonnet (4 tests, 27 examples) and Opus
(happy-path 16 examples) with **ExpectedToolCalled=1** and **Sequence Accuracy≈1**, the
operator rejected the result as PR proof because **`TRACING_ES_URL` was unset**:

> "evals without traces are not proof for anything … we need traces in golden cluster,
> because it's the only way to attach it to the PR as proof before/after"

## Why non-trace metrics are insufficient

When `TRACING_ES_URL` / `TRACING_ES_API_KEY` are absent, trace-based evaluators
(**Skill Invoked**, **Trajectory**) return **0** or `null` — not because routing failed,
but because the harness cannot query spans. Deterministic tool-call metrics
(`ExpectedToolCalled`, `Sequence Accuracy`, `ToolUsageOnly`) can look green while
reviewers still have no attachable OTLP evidence.

This is especially critical for **core Agent Builder platform tools** (`generate_esql`,
`execute_esql`, `search`) where platform reviewers will ask for span-level before/after
proof, not aggregate pass/fail.

## Required workflow

1. **Preflight** — confirm eval runner log shows `TRACING_ES_URL present: true` and the
   URL answers (golden ES `kbn-evals-serverless-ed035a`, not Scout `:9220`).
2. **Wire export** — use full `node scripts/evals run --profile dev-vault` (not
   `--export-profile` alone); see `feedback_matrix_local_export_dev_vault_profile.md`.
   For **waterfall UI** in Kibana APM/Discover: copy gitignored `config.json` from main
   `~/Projects/kibana` checkout into the worktree's `scripts/vault/` (never commit secrets);
   run with `--export-profile config`. Scout `:9220` traces are ephemeral and lost on stack
   restart — not suitable for post-hoc waterfall analysis.
3. **Kibana OTLP export** — local Scout Kibana must send traces to the same golden cluster
   (`telemetry.tracing.exporters` → golden `/_otlp`); eval runner reads them back via
   `TRACING_ES_URL`.
4. **Suite-specific trace client** — custom `traceEsClient` fixtures (e.g. AD2 suite
   `evaluate.ts`) must pass `auth: { apiKey: process.env.TRACING_ES_API_KEY }`; overriding
   the base fixture without auth causes golden-cluster `_query` failures even when parent
   env vars are set.
5. **Before/after package** — baseline run on `upstream/main` blob + candidate run on the
   same suite/model; capture golden trace IDs, score docs, and `evaluation.diff-runs` /
   `diagnose.misroute-signature` output for the PR description.
6. **Never declare routing fixed** from local runs that only show `ExpectedToolCalled=1`
   with `Skill Invoked=0` / `Trajectory=0` and no trace ES.

## Context: Option C (`generate_esql` boundary clause)

Jul 12 local verification of RFC `elastic/security-team#18054` Option C cleared
tool-call metrics on Sonnet+Opus but remained **evidence-incomplete** until golden-trace
reruns land. Structural subtractive binding (RFC) is still the durable fix; Option C is a
near-term stopgap pending full-catalog regression + golden traces.

## Never

- Treat a passing local eval as merge-ready for a shared platform tool without golden
  trace export configured and verified.
- Cite `Skill Invoked=0` / `Trajectory=0` as a routing regression when the runner log
  shows missing `TRACING_ES_URL`.

name: feedback_kbn_evals_http_handler_retry_shortcircuit
description: kbn-evals inference/prompt path has zero retries by default — httpHandlerFromKbnClient passes retries:0 which short-circuits wrapKbnClientWithRetries
type: feedback
---

# kbn-evals Inference HTTP Path Has Zero Retries By Default

In `@kbn/evals`, the inference REST client (used by non-agent-builder suites like
`significant-events`, `observability-ai`, `workflows`) rides through
`x-pack/platform/packages/shared/kbn-evals/src/utils/http_handler_from_kbn_client.ts`,
which calls `kbnClient.request({ ..., retries: 0 })`. That `retries: 0` is a
**trap**: `wrapKbnClientWithRetries` (`kbn_client_with_retries.ts`) explicitly
**no-ops its 6-attempt `withRetry` when `params.retries === 0`**:

```ts
if (params?.retries === 0) {
  return doRequest();   // bypasses withRetry entirely
}
```

So the wrapper layer does nothing for this path. `httpHandlerFromKbnClient`'s own
retry loop was then gated on `KBN_EVALS_HTTP_RETRIES ?? '0'` (default 0) **and**
only retried numeric statuses `{429,503,504}`. A dropped keep-alive socket
surfaces as `KbnClientRequesterError` with `status = N/A` (`typeof status !==
'number'`), so it was never retried even when retries were enabled. Net: a single
transient `fetch failed` / `SocketError: other side closed` under full parallel
weekly load failed the **whole eval example** (`attempt=1/0` in the log is the
tell — kbnClient's own 0-retry counter).

**Why:** Cost real debugging time on the weekly LLM-eval matrix branch — the
"random" `significant-events` / `observability-ai` failures looked like EIS
saturation but were actually zero-retry transport blips on the inference path.
Hardening `agent_builder_client.ts` (converse) did NOT cover this, because the
inference/prompt path is a different client.

**How to apply:**
- When an `@kbn/evals` suite fails with `[POST /internal/inference/prompt]
  request failed (attempt=1/0) ... fetch failed / other side closed`, it's the
  zero-retry inference transport, not a logic bug and not (only) EIS.
- The fix belongs in `httpHandlerFromKbnClient` (its own self-contained loop):
  default `maxRetries` ≥ 3, add `502`, and retry transport-level errors
  (`typeof status !== 'number'`) in addition to retryable statuses. 4xx stay
  terminal. No double-retry risk because the wrapper is bypassed on `retries:0`.
- `agent_builder_client.ts` (agent-builder converse) is a SEPARATE path; hardening
  one does not harden the other.

**Never:**
- Assume `wrapKbnClientWithRetries` protects every `kbnClient.request` — it
  self-disables on `retries: 0`, which the inference handler always passes.
- Attribute inference-path socket closes purely to EIS saturation without
  checking the retry count in the error (`attempt=1/0` = zero retries).

**Confirmed approach:** Landed on `fix/weekly-evals-matrix` (kibana) commit
`2930ad2d` — default 3 retries + transport-error retry in
`http_handler_from_kbn_client.ts`. Quality-preserving (only rescues transient
blips; cannot turn a passing test red).

# Keep cohort-isolated kbn-evals suites in separate packages

## Decision (Jul 13 2026)

**No** — do not merge `kbn-evals-suite-attack-discovery` and
`kbn-evals-suite-attack-discovery-agent-builder` into one package.

## Why the surfaces differ

| Suite | Entry point | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| Legacy `kbn-evals-suite-attack-discovery` | `runAttackDiscovery` / direct pipeline | Pipeline output quality |
| AD2 `kbn-evals-suite-attack-discovery-agent-builder` | Agent Builder `converse` API | Agent/skill orchestration, workflow evidence, tool efficiency |

- **Copy/import** shared quality evaluators (`AttackDiscoveryBasic`, `AttackDiscoveryCriteria`, optional `Rubric`) into the AD2 suite — no cross-package dependency yet.
- Port expected `attackDiscoveries` / `criteria` from legacy dataset into AD2 fixtures.
- Extract `kbn-evals-attack-discovery-common` **only** when the shared evaluator surface grows large enough to justify a new boundary.

type: feedback

source: kbn-evals workflow-guardrails-negative-eval session (Jul 10 2026)
---

# Matrix report has no default branch/CI scoping, even though provenance data already exists

An incident where an incomplete/local negative-test dataset's scores leaked into what looked like the published weekly matrix was traced to a structural gap, not a one-off fluke.

**The provenance data already exists** on every eval score document:
- `metadata.git.branch`, `metadata.git.commit_sha` — from `git rev-parse`, falling back to `BUILDKITE_BRANCH`/`BUILDKITE_COMMIT` (`x-pack/platform/packages/shared/kbn-evals/src/utils/git_metadata.ts:1-24`)
- `metadata.ci.build_id`, `build_url`, `pipeline_slug`, `pull_request`, `branch`, `commit` — from Buildkite env vars, only populated when actually running in CI (`ci_metadata.ts`)
- `metadata.execution_id` — CI runs: `bk-<BUILDKITE_BUILD_ID>::<modelId>`; local/experimental runs: whatever ad-hoc prefix the local script sets (e.g. `local-matrix-*`)

So a document from the weekly main-branch job is already distinguishable from a feature-branch/local experiment run: `metadata.ci` presence at all means "ran in real CI", and `metadata.git.branch == 'main'` + a known weekly `pipeline_slug`/`build_url` pins it to "the golden job" specifically.

**Root cause of the incident:** `generateMatrixReport` (`matrix_aggregation.ts:741-743`) defaults to a bare 14-day time window across **all** indexed docs, with **zero automatic branch/CI scoping**. Any local or feature-branch run within the last 14 days is aggregated into the same report as the golden weekly job, with nothing distinguishing them by default.

**Implication:** don't assume a matrix report number is "the golden weekly result" just because it renders in the standard report — verify `metadata.ci.pipeline_slug`/`metadata.git.branch` on the underlying docs, or add explicit branch/CI filters to the report query, before treating a number as production-representative. The fix direction is to make `generateMatrixReport` filter by default (main-branch + known weekly `pipeline_slug`), not to add new provenance fields — the fields already exist and are unused.

## Shipped fix (Jul 11 2026, `agent-builder-skill-dev-cursor-plugin`, additive only)

Three small changes, no new abstraction (all three pass the anti-overengineering gate — existing
machinery, existing consumer, in-place):

1. **Warn-on-mixed-branch** — `queryGitMetadataFromScores` (`matrix_aggregation.ts:836-853`)
   already detects multiple distinct `git.branch` values in a report window but previously only
   ran when the caller had already CI-scoped the query. Now runs unconditionally and surfaces a
   warning when `gitBranches.length > 1` — this closes the "why didn't we know the window spanned
   branches" gap directly.
2. **`canonical: true` shorthand** on the `generate-matrix` MCP tool param (`evaluation.ts`) —
   shorthands to `gitBranch: 'main'` + the latest weekly `pipeline_slug` so callers don't need to
   know the exact filter incantation.
3. **`is_weekly` ingest field** — added to `common_attributes.schema.yaml` (OpenAPI/Zod request-body
   schema, regenerate `.gen.ts` via the package's `scripts/openapi/generate.js`, NOT hand-edited),
   threaded through `ci_metadata.ts` (`KBN_EVALS_WEEKLY` env var → `is_weekly: true` in the outgoing
   Buildkite metadata payload). No change needed to `build_ingest_request.ts` since
   `buildkiteMetadata` is typed as `BuildkiteCiMetadata = BuildkiteMetadata`, which already picks up
   the new field structurally.

**Confirmed safe for the golden cluster (no mapping/template change):**
`scores_index_template.ts` (the file that actually defines the ES data-stream mapping) was read but
NOT touched. `metadata.ci` in that template has no `dynamic: false`/`strict` set, so a new
`is_weekly: boolean` field gets picked up by Elasticsearch's **dynamic mapping** on first ingest —
no explicit template PUT, no index-definition version bump, no coordinated migration needed. This
is the general pattern for adding new `metadata.ci.*`/`metadata.git.*` fields to eval score docs:
check the index template's `dynamic` setting before assuming a mapping change is required.

**Follow-up gap identified (not yet closed as of Jul 11 2026):** `is_weekly` was shipped as
ingest-only — it isn't yet wired into `canonical: true` as a filter, and `checkRegression`/
`getBaseline` (`trends.ts:98-315`) take a single `branch` param used for both "find latest run" and
"compute baseline", so they can only do rolling self-comparison today, not a cross-branch (feature
branch vs. main) regression check. Two more additive fixes proposed in the same session: a
`baselineBranch` param on `checkRegression`/`getBaseline`, and wiring `isWeekly` into `canonical: true`'s query.

name: feedback_kbn_evals_phantom_baseline_commit_sha
description: For kbn-evals baselines, verify both runtime commit identity and component provenance; a candidate-off feature branch can still contain unmerged skill hardening and cannot establish current-main behavior
type: feedback
confidence: strong
updated: 2026-07-11
source: kibana-worktrees-weekly-evals-matrix transcript 39a259da — RFC #18054 Option C baseline-comparison investigation
---

# "Phantom baseline" bug: trust ES-recorded commit metadata, not working-tree assumptions

## The pattern

While investigating whether a tool-description change (RFC #18054 Option C) caused
eval regressions, every prior "baseline" (pre-change) evaluation run turned out to have
actually executed against a Kibana dev server that ALREADY had Option C's change applied
— so there was no true baseline to compare against, and the apparent regressions were an
artifact of comparing patched-vs-patched runs.

## Why it happened

Kibana's dev-server (`scripts/kibana --dev`) file watcher restarts the server on any
source save. A previous eval run had already been kicked off against the Option-C-patched
server before the investigating session made any edit of its own — so grepping `git log`
for the file's history told the agent nothing about what description the *running
process* actually served at the time each prior run executed. Git history answers "what
changed in the working tree," not "what code was the live server process running."

## The fix / durable lesson

For any eval run against a dev-server-backed stack (as opposed to a fresh CI build):

- **Do not infer what code a past run exercised from `git log` / working-tree diff
  timing.** The dev server can be running code from before or after your own edits,
  independent of when you made them.
- **Cross-reference `metadata.git.commit_sha`** (embedded in every score document in the
  `.evaluation-scores` index at write time — see
  `x-pack/platform/packages/shared/kbn-evals/src/utils/git_metadata.ts`) against the
  wall-clock time of each Kibana server restart to determine which commit/patch state
  a given run's results actually reflect.
- Only trust a run as a "true baseline" once you've confirmed via `commit_sha` (or an
  explicit clean-checkout run) that the server was NOT running your candidate change at
  the time.

## Generalizable rule

For dev-server-backed evals, use ES-recorded commit metadata to identify the
repository snapshot that produced a score. Never infer it from the working-tree
state at the time you think the run started.

Commit identity is necessary but **not sufficient** for a causal baseline:

- A clean candidate-off run on a feature branch is a branch control, not a
  current-main baseline if that branch carries other unmerged prompt/skill/tool
  changes.
- Before attributing a score delta, check `git log -- <target files>` between the
  incident commit and test base, verify suspected fixes with
  `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fix> upstream/main`, and compare exact blob IDs
  with `git rev-parse <ref>:<path>`.
- Persist a content-addressed provenance manifest with each matrix run: repo
  SHA/dirty hash, target skill and inline-tool hashes, default prompt/tool
  catalog hashes, dataset/evaluator hashes, runtime config, and model IDs.
- Call a comparison causal only when all non-candidate hashes match. A
  current-main run answers current behavior; it cannot by itself prove what
  caused or fixed a historical incident.

**Confirmed incident:** During RFC #18054 Option A/B/C evaluation, the purported
"true baseline" had Option C removed but still contained five branch-only
`find-security-rules` hardening commits. Those commits appeared in local file
history but were not ancestors of `upstream/main`; the run therefore could not
answer whether current main still exhibited the original ES|QL misroute.

# Running a real kbn-evals suite against an EDD capsule / dev cell

The capsule (`boot-edd-capsule.sh`) only BOOTS the stack (ES+EDOT+Kibana on cell ports)
and writes `.edd-capsule/active.json`. It does NOT run the suite. Run suites yourself with
`node scripts/evals`.

## Point the suite at the cell's non-standard ports
kbn-evals uses Scout to discover Kibana/ES. For a cell on custom ports (not 5601/9200),
create `<worktree>/.scout/servers/local.json` (schema in
`kbn-scout/src/types/test_config.schema.ts`):

```json
{
  "serverless": false,
  "http2": true,
  "isCloud": false,
  "cloudUsersFilePath": "<worktree>/.ftr/role_users.json",
  "license": "trial",
  "hosts": { "kibana": "http://localhost:<kbnPort>", "elasticsearch": "https://localhost:<esPort>" },
  "auth": { "username": "elastic", "password": "changeme" }
}
```
- `cloudUsersFilePath` must be a non-empty path (default is `<repo>/.ftr/role_users.json`);
  create it as `{}` — not read for local stateful, but schema-validated.
- Also export `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` for the run (self-signed cell ES).
- **Separate gotcha for direct ES-client test helpers (not just Scout/synthtrace):**
  `createEsClientForTesting` (used by ad-hoc verification scripts, not the Scout-driven
  suite itself) reads its CA from `TEST_CA_CERT_PATH`, not `CA_CERT_PATH` or
  `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`. Kibana's dev ES cell containers auto-generate their own
  self-signed CA distinct from the shared `kbn-dev-utils` test CA, so point
  `TEST_CA_CERT_PATH` at the cell's actual `http_ca.crt` (extract it from the container)
  before minting an API key or querying ES directly in a verification script — otherwise
  the client fails cert validation even with `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` set for the
  main suite run.

## Command (env matters — trace-based evaluators need all of it)
```bash
KBN_EVALS_SKIP_CONNECTOR_SETUP=true NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 \
CI_STATS_DISABLED=true \
TRACING_EXPORTERS='[{"http":{"url":"http://localhost:4318/v1/traces"}}]' \
TRACING_ES_URL='https://elastic:changeme@localhost:<esPort>' \
node scripts/evals run --suite smoke-tests \
  --model eis-openai-gpt-4-1-mini --judge eis-anthropic-claude-4-5-sonnet \
  --grep "score ingestion|llm-judge|trace-retrieval"
```
- Use `run` (not `start`) when the stack is already up — `run` does no service management.
- **`--skip-server` is a `start`-only flag; passing it to `run` errors** ("Unknown flag").
- `KBN_EVALS_SKIP_CONNECTOR_SETUP=true` reuses the cell's preconfigured `eis-*` connectors
  (from `xpack.actions.preconfigured`) instead of trying to create/tear down connectors.
- `--model` / `--judge` take connector IDs; `node scripts/evals list [--json]` lists suites.
- **`TRACING_EXPORTERS` is REQUIRED for trace-based evaluators** (token/latency/tool-calls/
  skill-invocation). Without it the worker never inits a tracer → `getCurrentTraceId()`
  returns all-zeros → "Invalid traceId 000…0" → those evaluators are N/A. `run` does NOT
  set it (only `start` does via profiles). Also needs the EDOT TLS fix
  (feedback_edot_capsule_trace_tls_drop) and `trace.id`→`trace_id` in the evaluator ES|QL.
- **`CI_STATS_DISABLED=true`** — otherwise a passing run still exits 1 because the
  `CiStatsReporter.timings` post-step fails on an unreachable/self-signed CI-stats endpoint
  (`ci_stats_reporter.ts:141` gates on this env). Set it for clean exit codes in the queue.

## smoke-tests suite composition (good validation target)
1. `score ingestion and code evaluator` — inference + CODE evaluator + score ingestion
2. `llm-judge` — inference + LLM-as-judge (Criteria)
3. `trace-retrieval` — trace-based token evaluator (needs EDOT traces in `traces-*`)
4. `es-snapshot-loader` — replays a GCS snapshot; **needs `GCS_CREDENTIALS`, will fail
   without** → grep it out for a no-creds run.

## Unattended runs
Drop a `.task.sh` into the launchd job queue (i9: `~/i9-runner/queue/`; m1max:
`~/m1max-runner/queue/`); the runner logs to `<runner>/logs/<ts>_<name>.log` (+`.exit`) and
moves the task to `done/` (rc 0) / `failed/` (rc≠0). Runner picks up `*.task.sh` every ~10s.
The trailing `CiStatsReporter` axios/TLS error at end of a `run` is harmless CI telemetry
(silence with `CI_STATS_DISABLED=true`).

## Two gotchas when running via the runner queue (validated on m1max, Jul 3 2026)
1. **Node version**: the runner loads nvm's `default` (v22 on m1max), but Kibana pins its
   version via the worktree `.nvmrc` (v24.14.1) → `node scripts/evals` dies with "Kibana does
   not support the current Node.js version". `nvm use` inside the non-interactive runner
   subshell is unreliable — instead derive the version and prepend the bin to PATH directly:
   `NODE_VER=$(tr -d ' \tv' < "$WT/.nvmrc"); export PATH="$NVM_DIR/versions/node/v$NODE_VER/bin:$PATH"`.
2. **Connector list must be discoverable**: `getAvailableConnectors()`
   (`@kbn/gen-ai-functional-testing/src/connectors.ts`) reads connectors from the
   `KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS` env (base64 JSON `{id:{name,actionTypeId,config,secrets?}}`)
   OR from `config/kibana.dev.yml`'s `xpack.actions.preconfigured`. **`scripts/eis` creates the
   `.inference` connectors via API, so they are in NEITHER source** → `createPlaywrightEvalsConfig`
   throws "Evaluation connector id <id> was not found, pick one from " (empty list). Fix: build
   the env from the live API in the task:
   `export KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS=$(curl -s -u elastic:changeme -H 'kbn-xsrf: true' -H 'x-elastic-internal-origin: kbn' http://localhost:<kbn>/api/actions/connectors | python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64;c=json.load(sys.stdin);print(base64.b64encode(json.dumps({x["id"]:{"name":x.get("name",x["id"]),"actionTypeId":x["connector_type_id"],"config":x.get("config") or {}} for x in c if x.get("connector_type_id")==".inference"}).encode()).decode())')`.
   Connector IDs on the cell look like `.openai-gpt-4.1-mini-chat_completion`,
   `.anthropic-claude-4.6-sonnet-chat_completion` (NOT the memory's older `eis-*` naming).

## Validated result + the trace-indexing gap (m1max, Jul 3 2026)
With both fixes, smoke-tests ran clean: **`score ingestion and code evaluator` PASS (mean 1)
and `llm-judge` (Criteria) PASS** — real inference + LLM-as-judge work E2E on the cell. But
**`trace-retrieval` FAILED**: Input/Output-Tokens evaluators query `traces-*` by trace id and
get `verification_exception` because **`traces-*` never populates**. Isolation done: EDOT is
up + correctly configured (otlp 4317/4318 receivers, ES exporter → `host.docker.internal:9241`
with `insecure_skip_verify:true`, `mapping.mode:otel`), `host.docker.internal` resolves and ES
is curl-reachable from inside the container, ES has the OTel templates
(`traces-otel@template`), and a synthetic OTLP span POST to `:4318` returns HTTP 200
`partialSuccess:{}` — yet nothing lands in ES and the collector logs NOTHING (no export/error).
Leading suspect (WRONG, see below): the `elasticapm` processor dropping spans.

### ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (m1max, Jul 3 2026) — dual Docker runtime port hijack, NOT Kibana
After a long detour blaming Kibana (SDK version mismatch, `recordException` warnings, missing
`send_to_self` config — ALL WRONG), the real cause was infrastructure: a **rogue
`kibana-edot-collector` running in the OrbStack docker context** (alongside the intended colima one),
`restart=unless-stopped`, publishing `0.0.0.0:4318`. OrbStack won the host `:4318` bind before
colima's Lima mux, so ALL OTLP (Kibana server + eval worker + a raw OTLP probe) hit **OrbStack's**
collector, which had no path to the colima `es-edd-runner` the eval reads. Colima's EDOT never
received a span → `traces-*` empty, zero errors anywhere (exporter got 200 from OrbStack).
**FIX:** `docker --context orbstack rm -f kibana-edot-collector` +
`docker --context colima restart kibana-edot-collector`. Verified: real OTLP probe `traces-* 0→501`,
then smoke-tests `trace-retrieval` **PASSES** (`1 passed (34.4s)`, rc=0; `traces-*` grows during run).
**Decisive diagnostic:** emit ONE *real* OTLP span with the worktree's own exporter (NOT curl'd JSON,
which parses 0 spans and proves nothing); if it flushes yet `traces-*` stays 0, run
`lsof -nP -iTCP:4318 -sTCP:LISTEN` to see which process owns the port (OrbStack Helper vs colima
`...colima/ssh.sock [mux]`), and `docker context ls` + per-context `ps` to find duplicate containers.
The `trace-retrieval` evaluator now WORKS on this cell. Full writeup + retracted hypotheses:
`feedback_kibana_otlp_trace_export_not_delivering.md`.

**CORRECTION (Jul 4 2026) — the trace-STATS family is NOT fixed; earlier "all trace evaluators work"
was overstated.** A real agent-builder run (`--suite agent-builder --grep "product documentation"`)
shows the quality evaluators (Factuality/Relevance/Groundedness/Precision@10/Recall@10/F1/ToolCalls/
SkillInvocation) PASS, but the trace-STATS evaluators fail for TWO DISTINCT reasons:
- **Latency = indexing LAG.** `kbn-evals/src/evaluators/trace_based/factory.ts` retries only 5× (~1 min
  total, minTimeout 2s factor 2 cap 60s). The converse trace lands in `traces-*` but AFTER that budget:
  during the run `WHERE trace.id==<id>` returns 0 rows ("No data found for trace"); minutes later the
  same traceId shows 55–71 spans and `MAX(duration)` is present. So Latency would pass if data arrived
  in time — pure timing on a loaded cell.
- **Tokens = trace-context CORRELATION SPLIT (the real bug).** Input/Output/Cached Tokens do
  `FROM traces-* | WHERE trace.id==<converseId> | STATS SUM(attributes.gen_ai.usage.*_tokens)`. The
  inference `ChatComplete` spans DO carry `gen_ai.usage.*_tokens` (verified: 83 such spans in traces-*,
  ~20k tokens) and ARE produced during the agent-builder run — but under a DIFFERENT trace.id than the
  agent-builder `converse` trace (converse tree = agent/tool/HTTP/ES spans under one id; ChatComplete
  inference spans under separate ids like 790d87ef…/8b4bd578…, same run timestamps). So the SUM over the
  converse traceId is null → token evaluators fail. NOT a delivery/routing failure (data is in the RIGHT
  index, traces-generic.otel-default). **`send_to_self:true` is NOT the fix and flipping it is the WRONG
  lever** — the cell config comment documents send_to_self:true was added because "Without send_to_self:
  true, Skill Invoked reads 0", and it works (Skill Invoked PASSES in the run). send_to_self controls
  where the agent-builder's OWN spans export (→ they carry the converse trace.id, so skill-invocation
  correlates); the INFERENCE `ChatComplete` spans travel a SEPARATE tracer and get their own trace.ids
  regardless of this toggle. So flipping to false would REGRESS skill-invocation without fixing tokens.
  The real bug is upstream Kibana instrumentation: the agent-builder converse path does not propagate its
  trace context into the inference client calls, so `ChatComplete` spans never join the converse trace.
  Proper fix = context propagation in the agent-builder→inference boundary (a code change for the
  Agent Builder team), OR make the token/latency evaluators correlate by something other than a single
  trace.id. Decisive diagnostic that cracked it: query the
  evaluator's EXACT ES|QL against a completed run's traceId, then `FROM traces-* | WHERE name=="ChatComplete"
  | KEEP @timestamp,   trace.id, attributes.gen_ai.usage.output_tokens | SORT @timestamp DESC` to see the
  token-bearing spans live under other trace.ids. Full analysis:
  `feedback_kibana_otlp_trace_export_not_delivering.md`.
- **Generality proven at the population level** (not product-doc-specific): across the whole index,
  converse traces (`name=="POST /api/agent_builder/converse"`) ∩ `ChatComplete` traces = **∅** (e.g. 4
  converse vs 30 ChatComplete, overlap 0). Every agent-builder run is affected — it's architectural.
- **DEFINITIVE root cause (Jul 4 2026) — TWO tracer providers → TWO namespaces → TWO trace.ids per run;
  the token data is NOT lost, the eval just queries the wrong id.** Each converse yields two disjoint
  traces: (a) `traces-generic.otel-default` has the GLOBAL HTTP route span `POST /api/agent_builder/converse`
  (trace.id e.g. `d26aeda…`, NO tokens) — this is the id the eval captures; (b) `traces-agent_builder.otel-default`
  has the agent-builder SELF-trace `Converse`/`ExecuteAgent`/`ChatComplete`/`Tool:…` (trace.id e.g.
  `6a656a02…`, WITH tokens). The self-trace is internally coherent (all `Converse` trace.ids == all
  `ChatComplete` trace.ids, 4/4), and `SUM(gen_ai.usage.*_tokens)`+`MAX(duration)` over the SELF id returns
  real values (out=2301 inp=205392 dur=16.0s). So the fix is to make the eval use the self-trace id OR make
  the agent-builder root span inherit the HTTP request context. **Code:** the agent-builder registers its OWN
  inference tracer provider in `x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/agent_builder/server/tracing/register_tracing.ts`
  (`initInferenceTracerProvider({processors:[AgentBuilderSpanProcessor→send_to_self ES exporter, EvalSpanProcessor,
  GlobalBridgeProcessor]})`); its `Converse` root is NOT parented to the router's `withActiveSpan('route handler')`
  HTTP span, so it starts a new trace root. Note `EXECUTION_ID_BAGGAGE_KEY` already flows via `EvalSpanProcessor` —
  a viable eval-side join key. **Filed:** elastic/kibana#276308 (with repro script + this analysis).
- **PROTOTYPE RESULTS (Jul 4 2026) — two intuitive fixes tried on the live cell, BOTH rejected; exact
  fix located.** `output.traceId` (what the evaluators query) comes from the converse RESPONSE body
  `trace_id`, set server-side in `add_round_complete_event.ts:387` via `getCurrentTraceId()` =
  `trace.getActiveSpan().spanContext().traceId` — i.e. the HTTP/route trace (route/tool/ES/security
  spans, `SUM(gen_ai.usage.output_tokens)=0`), NOT the inference self-trace where ChatComplete/tokens
  live. (1) Setting `BAGGAGE_TRACKING_BEACON_KEY='kibana.inference.tracing'=1` in `withAgentBuilderContext`
  (agent_builder plugin) so `createInferenceContext` wouldn't `trace.deleteSpan`/fork → NO effect,
  because in `execution_runner.ts` `executeAgent$`/`generateTitle` are constructed OUTSIDE `withConverseSpan`
  (line ~208) and only subscribed inside it; inference spans are created across async RxJS boundaries the
  synchronous context/baggage doesn't reach. (2) Adding the beacon to the eval's outbound W3C `baggage`
  header in `kbn-evals/src/utils/http_handler_from_kbn_client.ts` (which today only sends execution_id/
  experiment_id, and only when TEST_RUN_ID is set) → ALSO no effect (request baggage still doesn't reach
  the inference-root creation). Verified each time via `_search` agg over the run's output.traceId: 0
  ChatComplete, out_tokens 0; the ChatComplete spans kept their own forked trace.id. Dev-mode Kibana
  (`scripts/kibana --dev`) auto-reloads server edits (~3 min restart, log
  `/Users/mac/.cursor/agent-builder-skill-dev-logs/edd-capsule-kibana.log`); kbn-evals edits need NO
  restart (transpiled in the eval process). **Quickest correct fix (proposed, not yet done): return the
  Converse INFERENCE span's trace id as the converse `trace_id`** (capture `withConverseSpan`'s span
  `spanContext().traceId`, thread into the round-complete event instead of `getCurrentTraceId()`) — the
  inference self-trace is coherent (Converse/ExecuteAgent/ChatComplete/Tool all share it), so tokens+
  latency+toolCalls would all correlate at once. Both prototype edits were REVERTED (worktree clean).

  connectors) exported or `--judge` fails with `Evaluation connector id ... not found, pick one from `
  (empty). Posted as comments on #276308.
- **CORRECTED DEFINITIVE root cause (Jul 4 2026, supersedes the two bullets above) — `output.traceId`
  is the EVAL's own client trace, and the converse endpoint's trace is actually COHERENT in isolation.**
  Instrumented the live `Converse` span (logged `span.spanContext().traceId` + `round.trace_id` in
  `with_converse_span.ts`) and diffed an isolated `curl` call vs the eval harness:
  - The eval's `output.traceId` (e.g. `7fd26f12…`, `7372859b…`) is the **eval CLIENT distributed trace**:
    `_search` shows `scope.name` = `@kbn/evals` + `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-undici` + `kibana.http`,
    only route/security/tool spans, **0 ChatComplete, 0 tokens**. The eval's undici auto-instrumentation
    creates a client span for the converse POST and propagates traceparent; the server route span joins it.
  - The SAME run's inference self-trace (the `Converse` span id) is a DIFFERENT id (`abb61c60…` out=2022
    inp=102516 dur=8.98s; `960d6c48…` out=2094 inp=215427 dur=12.1s) — fully coherent (Converse/ExecuteAgent/
