# kbn-evals multi-model batch concurrency + disk-pressure gate

## Architecture decided (Kibana `elastic/kibana` + agent-builder-skill-dev-cursor-plugin PR #140)

Running multiple models against `kbn-evals` is done as: **one shared Scout (ES+Kibana) stack + one separate Playwright CLI process per model**, not one worker/Scout instance per model. `scripts/run-security-evals-batch.sh` already implemented this base pattern (boot Scout once, dispatch `node scripts/playwright` per model with `--skip-server`); the added feature was `BATCH_MODEL_CONCURRENCY` (env var, default serial) to cap how many of those per-model processes run at once, tunable to available host resources.

Wired through: `scripts/run-security-evals-batch.sh` (bash loop with a concurrency cap) and `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/resources/evaluation.ts` (`model_concurrency` schema on `evaluation.run-batch`).

## Disk-pressure pre-flight (`check_disk_pressure()`)

Root cause that motivated this: the shared Scout ES+Kibana instance died mid-run because the root volume hit 92% full (802GB/926GB used), and Elasticsearch refused merges ("insufficient disk space... available disk space is only [0] bytes"). One eval run hung forever (in-flight request to a server that vanished), a second got immediate `ECONNREFUSED` — both were victims of the dead shared stack, unrelated to the multi-process concurrency itself.

**Fix:** `check_disk_pressure()` runs once per batch (after ports are assigned, before the first `boot_stack &`), gated by `BATCH_MIN_FREE_DISK_PCT` (default `10`). Use **percentage of disk free**, not a flat GB floor — it must match Elasticsearch's own disk-based shard-allocation watermarks, which are percentage-of-disk, not absolute:

| Watermark | Used % | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `cluster.routing.allocation.disk.watermark.low` | 85% used (15% free) | stop allocating new shards to the node |
| `cluster.routing.allocation.disk.watermark.high` | 90% used (**10% free**) | actively relocate shards away — this is the default threshold used |
| `cluster.routing.allocation.disk.watermark.flood_stage` | 95% used (5% free) | forces affected indices **read-only** — the exact failure mode this session hit |

A flat GB floor doesn't scale with disk size and doesn't match what ES itself gates on — the check must fail at the same boundary ES would, before degrading into flood-stage read-only. Docker's `docker system df --format '{{.Reclaimable}}'` is logged as a best-effort secondary hint only (non-fatal) — the Colima VM's internal disk can be starved independently of host-fs space, which is a second, separate way Scout can die even when `df` on the host looks fine.

This same `check_disk_pressure()` helper should also be wired into `kbn-evals`' own `ensureScout`/`eval_stack.ts` startup path (not just the plugin's batch script) so a single-model `node scripts/evals start` gets the same guard — as of this session it only covered the batch runner.

## bash 3.2 empty-array gotcha (macOS system bash)

`set -euo pipefail` + expanding an empty array with `"${arr[@]}"` throws `unbound variable` on bash 3.2 (still the macOS system default `/bin/bash`). This bit the new `BATCH_MODEL_CONCURRENCY` loop's `next_pids` array, which can legitimately be empty when all in-flight models finish.

**Fix idiom** (safe on both bash 3.2 and modern bash):
```bash
active_pids=("${next_pids[@]+"${next_pids[@]}"}")
```
The `+` triggers parameter-expansion-if-set, side-stepping `nounset` on a genuinely-empty array. Apply this pattern to any `"${arr[@]}"` expansion (copy-back, `for x in "${arr[@]}"`, etc.) inside a `set -u` bash script that must run under the stock macOS bash.

## Stress-measured `BATCH_MODEL_CONCURRENCY` defaults (Jul 12 2026)

`parallel-experiments` stress test on M1 (`worker-m1max`, 4 cheap/standard EIS models,
`smoke-tests`, 1 rep each):

| concurrency | wall time | connector errors |
|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | 160 s | 0 |
| 2 | 81 s | 0 |
| 3 | 80 s | 0 |
| 4 | **41 s** | 0 |

M1 load stayed ~2, ~16 GB free RAM, 0 swap at concurrency 4.

**Defaults:**
- **M1 Max 64GB:** `BATCH_MODEL_CONCURRENCY=4`
- **M4 Max 48GB:** `BATCH_MODEL_CONCURRENCY=2` (conservative — M4 fresh-stack stress
  failed under memory pressure; re-measure only after freeing RAM/load)

**Anti-pattern:** do not run `parallel-experiments` stress tests against an existing
shared `kbn-evals-weekly` Scout stack on M4 — a stress attempt OOM-killed Kibana and
destabilized the weekly worktree.

## Related fix landed same session: workflow-authoring false-acceptance guardrails

Separately, Opus's `Rejection @ workflows` eval failures (4/9, avg 0.556) were traced to a **false-acceptance problem, not false-refusal**: Opus never over-rejects, but silently "fixes" contradictory/unsupported requests instead of naming the limitation — e.g. asked for both a manual AND scheduled trigger simultaneously, it emitted a workflow YAML containing both without flagging the contradiction; asked for real-time streaming aggregation (which ES|QL/the workflow engine can't do), it silently substituted a bounded 5-min scheduled query. Fix: added explicit unsupported-feature + contradictory-trigger guardrails to both `workflow_docs.ts` (feeds the actual generation agent's system prompt — the real load-bearing path) and `workflow_authoring_skill.ts` (the discovery-facing reference the outer conversational agent sees).

# kbn-evals Buildkite Connector Configuration

## What Buildkite accepts today

Selection knob is **`EVAL_MODEL_GROUPS`** (comma-separated model group slugs), not raw connector JSON.

| Format | Example | Source |
|--------|---------|--------|
| EIS | `eis/openai-gpt-5.4` | `generate_eis_connectors.js` |
| LiteLLM gateway | `llm-gateway/Kimi-K2.6` | `generate_litellm_connectors.js` |

`get_connector_ids.js` filters the generated connector map against `EVAL_MODEL_GROUPS`.

There is **no `openrouter/*` model group** in CI scripts.

## Weekly vs on-demand

**Weekly** (`kibana-evals-weekly-llm-evals`): model lists are **hardcoded per suite** in `.buildkite/pipelines/evals/llm_evals.yml`. Trigger env vars **do not override** step-level anchors — cannot inject arbitrary external connectors at trigger time.

**On-demand** (`kibana-evals-on-demand-llm-evals`): pass models at trigger:

```text
EVAL_SUITE_ID=security-ai-rules
EVAL_MODEL_GROUPS=eis/openai-gpt-5.4
EVAL_INCLUDE_EIS_MODELS=1
```

Still EIS + `llm-gateway/*` unless passthrough (below).

## Arbitrary connector map (on-demand only)

**`EVAL_CONNECTORS_PASSTHROUGH=1`** + base64 **`KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS`** skips LiteLLM/EIS auto-generation. Gated on **`KBN_EVALS_ON_DEMAND=1`** — weekly runs reject passthrough.

```text
EVAL_SUITE_ID=security-ai-rules,security-alert-triage
EVAL_CONNECTORS_PASSTHROUGH=1
EVAL_MODEL_GROUPS=my-subject-model
EVALUATION_CONNECTOR_ID=my-judge-model
KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS=<base64 JSON map>
```

Do **not** set `EVAL_INCLUDE_EIS_MODELS=1` / `FTR_EIS_CCM=1` for pure custom connectors.

Legacy benchmarker path: **`BENCHMARK_MODEL_ID`** + `KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS` (vLLM injection) — same skip-generation behavior, narrower intent.

**Local (supported today):** export `KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS`, run `node scripts/evals start --suite … --model <connector-id>`.

## Local runtime — full security matrix, one model

14 security-relevant weekly suites sequential on one Scout stack: **~8–14 hours** wall clock (+ 15–30 min initial boot, + snapshot restore overhead per suite).

Practical local tiers (`run-local-matrix-suite.sh`):

| Tier | Scope | Time |
|------|-------|------|
| `smoke` | 1 routing example | ~1 min |
| `run-fast` | grep slice (~8 examples) | ~5–10 min |
| `run-critical` | 6 matrix-critical suites | ~5–8 h |
| `export-all` | 8 `MATRIX_SUITES` | ~10–14 h |

Don't replicate full weekly locally for interactive iteration — use `run-critical` or 2–3 targeted suites, then on-demand BK overnight on i9/M1 for single-model full sweep.

## Caveats

- Build env size limits for large base64 connector maps — Vault-backed secret + job hook is the production shape
- API keys in plain build env are visible in BK job metadata — prefer Vault for shared use

# Workflow eval trajectory pattern (managed workflows)

## Problem

`createTrajectoryEvaluator` compares ordered tool IDs vs a golden `tool_sequence` (LCS). Works for converse/agent-chat evals where task output includes `steps[]` with tool metadata.

**Managed workflow suites** (e.g. `kbn-evals-suite-alert-analysis-workflow`) run Workflows API executions, not converse. `AlertAnalysisVerdict` exposes only classification + `traceId` — no `tool_id` steps. `getToolCallSteps()` does not apply.

## Design intent (alert-analysis)

The workflow pre-builds context (enrichment before `ai.agent`). The model under test should return a structured verdict **without calling tools**. Trajectory = **zero-tool contract** (golden path `[]`), not per-alert golden tool paths.

## Critical implementation detail

**Extract at task time, score at eval time.**

The Playwright executor **overwrites** `output.traceId` with the task span when evaluators run (`{ ...taskOutput, traceId }` in `kibana_evals_executor/client.ts`). Do not rely on `createTraceBasedEvaluator` + `output.traceId` for workflow traces.

Inside `workflow_task.ts`:

1. Read `execution.traceId` after workflow poll completes.
2. ES|QL `traces-agent_builder.*` for ordered TOOL spans (`attributes.elastic.inference.span.kind == "TOOL"`).
3. Stash `toolCallIds: string[]` (and `toolCallsUnavailable` when trace export missing) on the verdict **before** evaluators run.
4. Wire `createTrajectoryEvaluator` with golden `[]` — score 1 iff actual length 0.

Trajectory returns **N/A** when `TRACING_ES_URL` unset or spans never land; empty tool list with spans present = legitimate score 1.

## Suite location

Alert-analysis workflow evals live on PR **#277272** (`alert-analysis-workflow-evals`), **not** `#274606` (`fix/weekly-evals-matrix` infra).

## Matrix rollup

`security-alert-analysis-workflow` → matrix **C4** (Workflow Execution); L2 trajectory + L3 classification patterns in skill-dev `matrix_mapping.ts`.

name: reference_kibana_esql_query_shape_and_pr_deploy_trigger
description: Two Kibana-specific gotchas found while building the endpoint_forensic_analysis skill and deploying its PR to a serverless security project — esql.query() response shape convention, and how the kibana-deploy-project-from-pr mechanism actually fires
type: reference
---

# Kibana: `esql.query()` response shape + PR-based serverless deploy trigger

## `esql.query()` — don't pass `format: 'json'`, destructure `{ columns, values }` directly

The proven in-tree pattern for ES|QL queries from a Kibana server-side tool
(`x-pack/.../entity_analytics/inline_tools/risk_score/risk_score.ts`,
`asset_criticality.ts`) calls:

```ts
const result = await context.esClient.asCurrentUser.esql.query({ query });
const { columns, values } = result; // no `format` flag, no casts
```

Passing `format: 'json'` and casting the result (`result as { values?: ...; columns?: ... }`)
changes the response shape — a tool written that way can silently return an
empty result at runtime with no thrown error, since the shape mismatch fails
quietly rather than type-erroring. When writing a new inline/builtin tool
that runs ES|QL, grep for an existing in-tree caller of `esql.query(` in the
same plugin first and match its exact call signature rather than assuming
the client API from docs/memory.

## Serverless security project deploy from a Kibana PR is a Buildkite checkbox, not label-auto-fired

Labels like `ci:project-deploy-security` + `ci:project-persist-deployment`
only **configure** the deploy (which serverless flavor, whether it persists
after the build). They do NOT trigger it. The actual trigger is a checkbox
(`kibana-deploy-project-from-pr`) inside the Buildkite PR-bot's comment on
the PR — ticking it fires a `kibana-deploy-project-from-pr` build. The bot
resets the checkbox display after ticking (cosmetic, not a failure signal).
Deploy typically takes 15-25 min; poll the triggered build (not the PR
labels) for terminal state / the resulting deploy-URL comment.

## PATCH vs full redeploy (`ci:project-redeploy`)

`deploy.sh` branches on the `ci:project-redeploy` label:

- **Default (PATCH):** `ci:project-deploy-security` +
  `ci:project-persist-deployment` without `ci:project-redeploy` → PATCH the
  existing serverless project's `docker_image` field only. Operator preference:
  use PATCH as the default for routine pushes.
- **Escalation (delete+recreate):** `ci:project-redeploy` → delete the
  existing project, then create a fresh one with the new image. Use only when
  PATCH reports Buildkite success but the live Kibana pod never rolls (stale
  `build_hash`, missing newly-shipped tools). Tradeoff: new project ID,
  credentials, Fleet server — enrolled VMs and seeded data must be redone.

Verified Jul 16–17 2026 on Kibana PR #278636: two PATCH deploys left
`build_hash` on commit `d9d5179` while HEAD was `427986e`; full redeploy
with `ci:project-redeploy` provisioned a fresh project that picked up the new
image.

source: daybreak-spike worktree bootstrap on i9 (Intel macOS, kibana-i9), Jul 6 2026
---

# Kibana main on Intel macOS: the moon 2.1.0 bootstrap blocker

## Symptom
`yarn kbn bootstrap` on an Intel (x86_64) Mac dies immediately at the moon step:
```
Error: Cannot find module '@moonrepo/core-macos-x64/package.json'
    at findMoonExe (node_modules/@moonrepo/cli/utils.js:43)
code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'
```
Not a memory/RAM problem — it fails in seconds, before any heavy work.

## Root cause
Kibana main pins `@moonrepo/cli@2.1.0` (root package.json direct devDependency, and it's
the resolved top-level). moon **2.1.x dropped the macOS-Intel binary**: on npm,
`@moonrepo/core-macos-x64` versions jump `2.0.0-canary…` → `2.2.0` (there is NO 2.1.x).
moon 2.2.0 release notes: "Temporarily brought back x86_64-apple-darwin (Apple Intel) as a
supported operating system." Apple Silicon (arm64) is unaffected — `core-macos-arm64@2.1.0`
exists, so M1/M2/M3/M4 Macs bootstrap fine with no override.

## Fix (override @moonrepo/cli to 2.2.6)
Two edits to root `package.json` — BOTH required. A bare `resolutions` entry alone does
NOT override a direct dependency in yarn classic (it created a duplicate lock entry while
node_modules still got 2.1.0):
1. `resolutions`: add `"@moonrepo/cli": "2.2.6",`
2. direct devDependency: change `"@moonrepo/cli": "2.1.0"` → `"2.2.6"`
Then `yarn kbn bootstrap --force-install`. A plain re-run is skipped by the yarn.lock
integrity check ("no need to update"); `--force-install` re-resolves, rewrites yarn.lock,
and pulls `@moonrepo/core-macos-x64@2.2.6`. Delete `node_modules/@moonrepo` first so the
stale 2.1.0 cli is replaced cleanly.

Verified on kibana-i9: moon 2.2.6 runs natively on Intel, bootstrap exits 0 (~150s on a
warm tree), `core-macos-x64` installed.

## Compat note (why 2.2.6 is safe)
moon 2.2.0's ONLY breaking change is the `--json` node format for `project-graph` /
`task-graph` / `action-graph` (nodes are now integers + a separate `data` object). It does
NOT touch `moon query`. Kibana's `@kbn/moon` only invokes `moon query` (query projects /
touched-files) — confirmed via `moon query projects` returning valid JSON on 2.2.6. Stay in
the 2.2.x line (2.2.6 = latest 2.2 patch) to minimize drift from Kibana's intended 2.1.0.

## Durability
- Local delta = `package.json` + `yarn.lock` only. MUST stay out of any feature commit/PR.
- Any rebase/pull from main reverts the bump → re-breaks bootstrap. Idempotent re-apply
  script on the i9: `~/reapply-moon-x64-override.sh` (patches package.json if needed +
  --force-install).
- No upstream fix imminent: NO open Kibana PR bumps moon to 2.2+. Only stale Renovate PRs
  within the Intel-broken 2.1.x line — #261214 (v2.1.1, main) and #263653 (v2.1.3, 9.4),
  both OPEN since April. Renovate groups `@moonrepo/cli` (minimumReleaseAge 14d,
  kibana-operations reviewers). Kibana likely holds at 2.1.x to avoid the 2.2.0 `--json`
  break, so Intel-mac stays collateral damage indefinitely.

## Fleet implication
Intel i9 (`kibana-i9`, 100.80.240.118) CAN host a Kibana-main dev worktree WITH this
override. Apple Silicon (M1 Max `worker-m1max` 100.67.93.90, M4) need no override. Note the
i9 also runs elastic-llm-benchmarker 24/7 — a long-running Kibana dev stack there competes
for its 32GB RAM.

# Local Scout Eval Boot Sequence (security-ai-rules)

Codifies the boot sequence that finally let `run-local-matrix-suite.sh`
validate the C2 L2 find-rules routing fix on a local stack
(Scout :5623 / ES :9223 / EDOT :4318). Two non-obvious traps.

## Trap 1 — Scout wipes ES on every `start-server`, so EIS must run AFTER the final boot

`node scripts/scout.js start-server` re-initialises Elasticsearch on each
start. So inference endpoints provisioned by `node scripts/eis` are **gone**
after any subsequent Scout reboot.

The two-pass local boot needs EIS in this order:

1. Boot Scout (no connectors baked).
2. `node scripts/eis` → provisions `.inference` endpoints in pass-1 ES.
3. Read endpoint ids from ES → build `KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS`
   (base64 of `{ ".<id>-chat_completion": {...} }`).
4. Reboot Scout with `KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS` baked +
   `KBN_EVALS_SKIP_CONNECTOR_SETUP=true`. **This reboot wipes ES → pass-1
   endpoints are gone.**
5. **Run `node scripts/eis` AGAIN** against the fresh pass-2 ES. Endpoint
   ids are deterministic, so the preconfigured `.inference` connectors baked
   in step 4 already reference the right ids.
6. Probe the connector, then run the suite.

Running EIS only before the reboot (step 2 without step 5) leaves the
preconfigured connectors pointing at wiped endpoints → converse calls 500.
`run-local-matrix-suite.sh` `cmd_stack_boot` now does step 5
(commit on `fix/local-scout-connector-boot`).

## Trap 2 — Python urllib cannot parse inline basic-auth in the URL

Handing `http://elastic:changeme@127.0.0.1:9223/...` to
`urllib.request.urlopen` fails with
`gaierror: nodename nor servname provided, or not known` — urllib treats the
whole `user:pass@host` as the hostname. Fetch with `curl` (which parses
inline creds), then let Python only transform the JSON. `curl -sf … -o file`
+ `python3 <file>` is the pattern `sync_connectors_env` already uses.

## Trap 3 — `KBN_EVALS_SKIP_CONNECTOR_SETUP` + already-provisioned endpoints

If the eval harness tries to CREATE an `.inference` connector for an endpoint
CCM already provisioned, Kibana returns
`500 … "Inference with id … already exists"`. Bake connectors at Kibana
startup via `KIBANA_TESTING_AI_CONNECTORS` and set
`KBN_EVALS_SKIP_CONNECTOR_SETUP=true` so the harness reuses them instead of
re-creating.

## Gotchas

- `SUBJECT_CONNECTOR` in ES-inference mode must be the connector id
  (`.anthropic-claude-4.6-sonnet-chat_completion`), NOT a legacy `eis-*` id —
  otherwise the post-boot probe never matches and stack-boot returns 1 on an
  otherwise-healthy stack.
- Cold Kibana boots here take ~6 min; the 180s default readiness wait is too
  short. `SCOUT_BOOT_WAIT_ITERS` (×2s) makes it configurable.
- Local Scout has no score ingest target (scores stay on ephemeral CI ES);
  local runs validate trajectory/skill-invocation via OTLP traces, not
  golden-cluster scores. On-demand CI + golden export remains the merge gate.

## Validated

Jul 2 session: with the corrected sequence, `security-ai-rules` routing
smoke (`routing-find-mitre-tag`, Sonnet 4.6) passed with Trajectory=1.0,
ForbiddenToolNotCalled=1.0, Skill Invoked (find-security-rules)=1.0 — the
C2 L2 fix confirmed on a live local stack.

# Loop Engineering Canvas (source reference)

[github.com/alindnbrg/loop-engineering-canvas](https://github.com/alindnbrg/loop-engineering-canvas) — a **design template** (not code), pushed 2026-07-04. A one-page canvas for designing an agentic loop *before* building it, plus four production-grounded worked examples. Analyzed and integrated 2026-07-05.

## Core thesis

Build the system that solves the problem, not the solution — "the thing that builds the thing." The **goal** (a definition of done something other than you can check) sits at the center; everything else serves it. **The goal bounds reuse:** a loop is trustworthy on the next case only as far as its check can verify it.

Loop model: `trigger → state → agent → effect → gate → control →` (loops back).

## The nine fields (worked outside-in)

Goal · Problem · Trigger (+concurrency) · Actions (scope/authority/isolation) · State · Limits · Control · Observability · Model & Prompt (last, swappable).

The four the 5-property audit doesn't cover: **Trigger/concurrency, Action scope+authority+isolation, Observability, Model-last swappability.**

## Three design principles (adopted)

1. **Deterministic engine does the work; the model only steers the rule** — the gate, not the model, is the source of truth; keeps the model mid-tier + swappable.
2. **The goal bounds reuse** — a narrow machine-checkable gate is what lets one loop travel across the class.
3. **Safety lives in the harness, not the prompt** — scope = `PermissionError`, kill switch at orchestration/RBAC layer, risky authority gated behind human approval.

## The four case studies

| Example | Deterministic engine | Model's only job | Gate | Archetype |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JVM dependency upgrade | OpenRewrite recipe | authors/refines `rewrite.yml` | `mvn verify` green | eval-fix-rerun (existing) |
| Salesforce incident ticket | runbooks + RBAC + SLO | picks next runbook | SLO green + case documented | gate-retry / poll-babysit (existing) |
| Test factory | mutation engine injects faults | drafts one test per mutant | fails on mutant, passes on HEAD | **mutation-verified generation (new)** |
| Vulnerability discovery | sandbox compiles + runs PoC | proposes bug; 2nd model disproves | PoC reproduces + survives refutation | **propose-prove-disprove (new)** |

Numbers worth remembering: IBM ITBench — top models resolve only **13.8%** of SRE scenarios end-to-end (→ scope loops to known classes, escalate the rest). Meta ACH — 9,095 mutants → 571 hardening tests, 73% engineer-accepted. Cloudflare Glasswing — adversarial validator cut first-pass rejection from 40%→11%.

## What it does NOT cover (kept from the 5 properties)

Regression guard (re-measure all dimensions after a fix), isolated one-category-per-iteration fixes, explore-vs-validate convergence modes. The canvas is a design snapshot, not a refinement engine.

## Related references (scope boundary)

- [reference_loop_engineering_patterns.md](reference_loop_engineering_patterns.md) — the **pattern taxonomy** (Reflexion, maker-checker, Ralph, convergence detection, three-loops diagnostic, treadmill mapping). This canvas ref is the **design surface + case studies**; keep technique/taxonomy material there, design-surface material here.
- `loop-first-approach` skill — the **five-property audit rubric + archetypes** (canonical); see [reference_loop_first_approach_skill_location.md](reference_loop_first_approach_skill_location.md).

- `~/.agents/rules/loop-engineering.md` — new "Deterministic-First Design" section.
- Analysis canvas: `~/.cursor/projects/empty-window/canvases/loop-engineering-canvas-analysis.canvas.tsx`.

# Loop Engineering Patterns (2026)

Comprehensive reference for designing agentic loops. Sources: Addy Osmani (Loop Engineering), AgentPatterns.ai (Three Loops), Evolve Loop, eval-loop, Conductor, Microsoft Agent Framework, Reflexion (Shinn et al. NeurIPS 2023).

**Scope boundary (avoid drift):** this file is the **pattern taxonomy** — the named techniques (Reflexion, maker-checker, Ralph, convergence detection) and the three-loops diagnostic. For the **whole-system design surface** (the 9-field canvas, goal-bounds-reuse, deterministic-engine-does-the-work, and the 4 production case studies) see [reference_loop_engineering_canvas.md](reference_loop_engineering_canvas.md). For the **five-property audit rubric + archetypes**, use the `loop-first-approach` skill (canonical; see [reference_loop_first_approach_skill_location.md](reference_loop_first_approach_skill_location.md)). Keep new taxonomy here; keep design-surface/case-study material in the canvas ref.

## Three Loops (Diagnostic Framework)

Every agent session is three nested loops. Observable symptoms route to the matching fix:

1. **Inner tool loop** (single turn): model + tool calls. Pathology = repeated identical calls. Fix = iteration cap.
2. **Verification loop** (across turns): external gates (tests, lint, build). Pathology = persistent red tests. Fix = sharper feedback (full traces, not summaries).
3. **Outer convergence loop** (across sessions): plan progress. Pathology = oscillating diffs / scope drift. Fix = revisit plan; use convergence signals (change velocity, output size, content similarity).

Tasks with deterministic tests collapse loops 2+3. Tasks without tests (prose, design) need convergence detection: two consecutive low-diff passes = converged, stop.

## Six Building Blocks

1. **Automations** — triggers (cron, hooks, CI) that make a loop repeat
2. **Worktrees** — isolated filesystems for parallel agents
3. **Skills** — reusable instruction sets (`SKILL.md`)
4. **Connectors** — MCP integrations (GitHub, Slack, Linear)
5. **Sub-agents** — federated workers; separate maker from checker
6. **Memory** — persistent state outside conversation (AGENTS.md, SQLite, files)

## Key Patterns

- **Reflexion**: after failure, generate structured first-person critique + store in episodic memory + prepend to next attempt. 34% quality uplift at 1.6x cost. Requires external failure signal.
- **Maker-Checker Split**: model that wrote code must not grade it. Use separate verifier model, test suite, or human gate.
- **Ralph Wiggum**: fresh context every iteration, state on disk. Prevents context rot in long-running tasks.
- **Journal-Driven Retry**: failure journal with structured context turns retries into directed search.
- **Convergence Detection**: change velocity + output size + content similarity. Always pair with hard max-round cap.
- **Durable Execution**: checkpoint after every LLM call or irreversible action. Resume from checkpoint, not start.

## Treadmill Mapping

| Pattern | Treadmill Implementation | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| Reflexion | constraint-generator (auto-derives constraints from recurring failures) | Could add per-job episodic reflection buffer |
| Maker-Checker | unified pipeline gates (separate from execution agent) | Gate models could be cross-family |
| Ralph Wiggum | fresh session per job, state in SQLite | Already implemented |
| Journal-Driven Retry | gate_failures table + constraint injection | Already implemented |
| Convergence Detection | pass-convergence narrative | Already implemented |
| Durable Execution | job-store + SQLite state machine | Already implemented |

## When to Suggest a Loop

Proactively suggest a loop when ANY of these triggers hold:
- Task will recur (weekly, per-PR, per-commit, per-deploy)
- Task has a deterministic success gate (tests pass, lint clean, build green)
- Task benefits from cross-attempt learning (same failure keeps happening)
- Task outlasts one context window
- Task runs while operator is not watching
- Task has a natural maker/checker split

## Anti-Patterns

- **Doom loops**: no external termination. Always cap iterations.
- **Self-grading**: agent evaluates own output. Use separate verifier.
- **Context rot**: all history in conversation. Externalize state.
- **Token spirals**: linear context growth. Summarize; cap episodic memory.
- **Comprehension debt**: code ships faster than audit. Keep human gate.

## Sources

- Osmani: addyosmani.com/blog/loop-engineering/
- AgentPatterns: agentpatterns.ai/agent-design/three-loops-agentic-coding/
- Convergence: agentpatterns.ai/agent-design/convergence-detection/
- Evolve Loop: github.com/mickeyyaya/evolve-loop
- eval-loop: gist.github.com/joctaTorres/1c0008a2581b8983a56e0dd9889afe4a
- Reflexion: Shinn et al. NeurIPS 2023; niteagent.com production build log
- Conductor: conductor-oss/conductor production-agent-architecture.md
- Harness Guide: genalphai.com/agentic-loops-and-harness-engineering/

# M1 Max Apple-Silicon EDD Runner — Deltas vs i9

Pairs with `reference_headless_macos_runner_setup` (the base recipe, validated on the Intel i9)
and `reference_dev_machine_fleet`. m1max = `worker-m1max` in `~/.ssh/config` (HostName
100.67.93.90, User `mac`, home `/Users/mac`). Everything the i9 got, m1max got — but Apple
Silicon changes several concrete steps:

## Path / arch differences
- **Homebrew is at `/opt/homebrew/bin/brew`** (not `/usr/local/bin/brew`). Every launch
  wrapper / runner / supervisor script must `eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"`.
- **No moon x64 shim needed.** arm64 is Kibana's first-class path — `yarn kbn bootstrap`
  just works (the `@moonrepo/core-macos-x64` gap in `feedback_kibana_intel_mac_moon_binary`
  is Intel-only). Bootstrap was ~3.5 min on the M1 Max/64GB.
- **GGUF is no-go on Apple Silicon MLX/LM Studio** — use MLX-native quant formats
  (MTP-5bit, OptiQ-4bit, etc.), not GGUF. Verified Jul 6 2026 when evaluating Ornith 35B
  alternatives for the M1 Max inference appliance.
- Runner dirs mirrored under `mac`'s home: `~/m1max-runner` (queue/logs/done/failed) +
  `m1maxctl.sh`; `~/m1max-setup` (launch wrappers, phase logs); launchd labels
  `com.m1max.edd-runner` + `com.m1max.edd-kibana`. Local copies in `~/m1max-runner-setup/`.
- Cell reuses the **same slot/ports as i9** (slot 41: ES 9241, Kibana 5642, EDOT 4318) —
  fine because ports are host-local. Boot with `boot-edd-capsule.sh --worktree <wt> --slot 41`.

## Spotlight is the #1 gotcha (not present in the i9 notes)
A fresh Kibana worktree (node_modules + rspack output = ~1M files) triggers a **Spotlight
indexing storm** — a swarm of `mdworker` + `mds` pushed load to ~40 on a 10-core box and
stalled Kibana's event loop for **13 s** (`kibanaUsageCollection` "event loop delay ...
13250ms"), so Kibana took 15-20 min to serve or looked hung at HTTP 000/503.
Fix: `sudo mdutil -a -i off` (disable indexing on all volumes). Also drop
`.metadata_never_index` markers in `~/Projects/kibana` and `~/Projects/kibana.worktrees`.
After disabling, load fell to ~2 and Kibana served in ~5 min. **Do this early** on any
Apple-Silicon dev runner.

## Docker CLI (brew formula, not Docker Desktop) needs a cred helper
`brew install docker docker-compose` gives a CLI whose `~/.docker/config.json` had
`"credsStore": "osxkeychain"` but the helper binary was missing → **even anonymous
`docker pull` failed** (`docker-credential-osxkeychain ... not found`). For a headless box,
`brew install docker-credential-helper` AND/OR just remove the `credsStore` key (auths was
empty) so pulls never touch the keychain (keychain access fails in non-interactive launchd
contexts anyway). Also `brew link --overwrite docker` if the formula installed unlinked.

## colima: ONE owner only
Running `colima start` manually **and** `brew services start colima` fights over the same
`~/.colima/default` VM — the brew launchd service errored and **tore down the running
containers** and left the docker daemon socket unreachable while `colima status` still said
"running". Recovery = `colima stop && colima start` (clean), then probe `docker ps` a few
times to confirm the daemon is stable. Decision: **do NOT use `brew services` for colima**;
let the `com.m1max.edd-kibana` launchd supervisor own it (`colima status || colima start`),
matching the i9 supervisor design. colima start: `--cpu 6 --memory 16 --disk 80 --vm-type vz`.
Cell ES/EDOT containers get `docker update --restart unless-stopped` so they auto-start once
colima's daemon is up after a reboot.

## `colima status` is flaky under concurrent calls — use `docker info` as the liveness invariant
A periodic health/smoke check that gates on `colima status | grep -qi running` throws intermittent
false `colima-down` alerts: `colima status` locks the Lima config and transiently errors when called
in quick succession (observed 1 OK / 2 false-fail across 3 back-to-back runs while colima was
genuinely up). Fix: only flag down if the **docker daemon is ALSO unreachable** — daemon reachability
is the invariant that actually matters:
```bash
if ! colima status 2>&1 | grep -qi running; then docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || problems+=("colima-down"); fi
```
Applied to `stack-smoke-check.sh` on both m1max and i9.

## zsh word-splitting bites remote loops
Default login shell for `mac` over SSH is **zsh**, which does NOT split unquoted `$var`.
`for kv in "disablesleep 1"; do sudo pmset -c $kv; done` sent pmset a single arg
"disablesleep 1" → "Usage" error. Run each `pmset` call explicitly, or `bash -c`, or use
`${=kv}`. Same class of bug: writing a sudoers file with `echo ... | (echo $PW | sudo -S tee
FILE)` wrote an **empty file** (the password pipe consumed tee's stdin) — use
`echo "$PW" | sudo -S sh -c 'echo "<rule>" > /etc/sudoers.d/<f>; chmod 0440 ...'` instead.

## Reboot-survival specifics applied (parity with i9)
- passwordless sudoers: `/etc/sudoers.d/m1max-nopasswd` = `mac ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL`
  (0440). (Machine also had a leftover `amphetamine_PowerProtect` sudoers + Amphetamine app
  actively preventing sleep — a second no-sleep layer.)
- no-sleep: `pmset -c {sleep,displaysleep,disksleep,powernap}=0`, `womp 1`, `autorestart 1`,
  and **`pmset -a disablesleep 1`** — note `disablesleep` is a *global* flag (set via `-a`),
  it does NOT appear in `pmset -g custom`; verify via `pmset -g | grep SleepDisabled` → 1.
- FileVault OFF via `fdesetup disable -inputplist` (Username `mac`), autologin via XOR
  `/etc/kcpassword` (11-byte key) + `defaults write .../com.apple.loginwindow autoLoginUser
  -string mac`. (kcpassword recipe in `reference_headless_macos_runner_setup`.)

## OrbStack + colima both installed → silent OTLP port hijack (trace-based evals broke)
m1max had **OrbStack installed alongside colima**. A stray `kibana-edot-collector` container was
running in the **OrbStack** context (from an earlier setup run against the OrbStack docker socket)
with `restart=unless-stopped`, publishing `0.0.0.0:4318` — and OrbStack won the host `:4318` bind
before colima's Lima mux could. Result: every OTLP export (Kibana server, eval worker, even a raw
OTLP probe) hit **OrbStack's** collector, never colima's EDOT → `traces-*` stayed empty, trace-based
evaluators failed, and NO error appeared anywhere (exporter got 200 from OrbStack). Wasted a long
detour on false Kibana-side theories (SDK version mismatch, `send_to_self` config).
FIX: `docker --context orbstack rm -f kibana-edot-collector` then
`docker --context colima restart kibana-edot-collector` (colima re-binds the freed port). Verified:
probe span `traces-* 0→501`, `trace-retrieval` eval PASSES. Diagnose with `lsof -nP -iTCP:4318
-sTCP:LISTEN` (shows the OWNING process — OrbStack Helper vs colima's `...colima/ssh.sock [mux]`) plus
`docker context ls` + per-context `ps`. LESSON: on any cell with >1 docker runtime, a container in the
"other" runtime can steal a published host port from the one you think you're using. Prefer ONE
runtime per headless cell. Full writeup: `feedback_kibana_otlp_trace_export_not_delivering.md`.

## Detach long remote jobs correctly
`macOS has no setsid`. Launching a long boot over a **non-multiplexed** SSH
(`-o ControlPath=none ... nohup ... &`) got the process **SIGTERM'd (exit 143)** when the
connection closed. Launch over the persistent multiplexed connection (ssh config
`ControlMaster auto` + `ControlPersist 600`) with `caffeinate -dimsu nohup ... </dev/null &
disown` — that survives. Use `-o ControlPath=none` only for quick *status* probes when the
master connection is congested by a busy box.

## End state (Jul 3 2026)
Kibana 200 on :5642 (launchd-supervised, single instance, supervisor idles when up),
ES green + EDOT collector (TLS `insecure_skip_verify`) on cell ports, **21 `.inference`
frontier connectors** (Anthropic/Google/OpenAI), 65 EIS inference endpoints, job-queue
runner live (`m1maxctl status`). Not yet reboot-validated at time of writing (i9 was).

# Reading Empty Security LLM Matrix Cells (real gap vs false gap)

When `generate-matrix` shows an empty / `·` cell, classify before treating it
as a gap. On weekly build #53 (`f80da75`) most "gaps" were by-design.

## L5 (Trace Observability) empty across EVERY category — REAL but NON-GATING

L5 token/toolCalls come from framework trace-based evaluators
(`x-pack/platform/packages/shared/kbn-evals/src/evaluators/trace_based/tokens.ts`)
which run:

```
FROM traces-* | WHERE trace.id == "<converse output.traceId>"
  | STATS SUM(attributes.gen_ai.usage.input_tokens)
```

Diagnosis fork that pins the cause:
- **L1 skill-invocation IS populated** → `traces-*` exists and carries the
  agent/skill spans, and the converse `output.traceId` linkage is correct
  (skill_invocation.ts queries the same index by the same trace id).
- **L5 token/toolCalls empty everywhere** → the `attributes.gen_ai.usage.*`
  (LLM usage) spans are NOT landing in `traces-*` in weekly CI.

So it is NOT a suite-wiring bug (security-ai-rules DOES wire
`evaluators.traceBasedEvaluators` + `traceEsClient` in both
`evaluate_dataset.ts` and `evaluate_routing_dataset.ts`) and NOT a matrix bug.
It is an EDOT / inference span-emission gap: the EIS/LLM calls' gen_ai usage
spans aren't collected into `traces-*` on the ephemeral Scout cluster the
evaluator queries. Related but distinct from
`feedback_edot_capsule_trace_tls_drop.md` (that one = traces-* fully empty via
TLS cert drop; here traces-* has skill spans, only usage spans missing).

**Non-gating:** `MATRIX_MANDATORY_INTERNAL_LAYERS = [L1,L2,L3]`,
`MATRIX_MANDATORY_EXTERNAL_LAYERS = [L3]`. L5 is not required for the composite
recommendation or the C1–C6 DoD. The token-cost customer HTML ranges
(skill-dev `matrix_token_cost_customer_html.ts`) populate only once L5 lands;
until then they degrade to median-only / null.

**Verify on a fresh run, don't assume:** run `evaluation.cost` on a new
on-demand run id — if it still returns 0 spans, the gap is systemic; fix lives
in the EDOT collector config for the weekly Scout stack + gen_ai span emission,
not in the suite or the matrix.

## C6 (Attack Discovery) — COMPLETE by design (only L3 populated)

Not a gap. `MATRIX_NOT_APPLICABLE_CELLS` marks C6 **L1/L2/L4 as N/A**
(runs via inference API not skill routing; no agent tool trajectory; direct
generation task = no tool selection/schema). L3 (Content Quality) is the only
applicable scored layer and IS populated. C6 is in `MATRIX_REPORT_CATEGORIES`.

## C7 (Automatic Migration) — DEFERRED by design (entirely empty)

Not a gap for the current DoD. `security-automatic-migrations` is in
`REPORT_EXCLUDED_SUITE_IDS` and C7 is NOT in
`MATRIX_REPORT_CATEGORIES = [C1,C2,C3,C4,C6]`. The DoD is explicitly **C1–C6**.
Re-include only once automatic-migrations evaluators are baselined in weekly CI.

## C5 (Multi-step) — EXCLUDED per operator

`security-multi-step` in `REPORT_EXCLUDED_SUITE_IDS` (HITL prompt-state failure
+ L4 evaluators not wired). Operator explicitly excluded C5 from weekly.

## The real gaps that DO need action

- **C2 L2 = 0** (Detection Engineering × Trajectory): genuine routing gap, not
  a false one — see `feedback_find_rules_routing_esql_fallback.md`. Fixed by
  tool-description routing (`557a50c`); confirm via fresh on-demand build.

# MCP App Tool Bridge (skill-dev-plugin)

Pattern for Cursor MCP App iframes (SEP-1865) when the server exposes resource tools `{ action, args }` but iframe `tools/call` needs flat JSON.

## Problem

Iframe poll loops cannot call `evaluation { action: "status" }` without a client-side adapter in every view build.

## Decision (eval-cockpit ADR)

Add **thin flat wrapper tools** that delegate to existing handlers via `dispatch()`. No duplicated eval logic.

| Wrapper | Delegates to | Poll? |
|---------|--------------|-------|
| `eval-cockpit-health` | `diagnose.health` | yes |
| `eval-cockpit-status` | `evaluation.status` | **yes — use for iframe** |
| `eval-cockpit-watch` | `evaluation.watch` | **no — blocks until terminal** |
| `eval-cockpit-failures` | `evaluation.failing-examples` | on demand |
| `eval-cockpit-split-signals` | `evaluateSplitSignals()` | on demand |
| `eval-cockpit-diff` | `evaluation.diff-runs` | on demand |

Each wrapper: `_meta.ui.visibility: ["app"]` so hosts hide poll helpers from model-visible tool list.

Entry tool `eval-cockpit` stays model-facing with `_meta.ui.resourceUri: ui://eval-cockpit/mcp-app.html`.

## Rejected alternatives

1. **Iframe adapter** mapping flat → `{ action, args }` — duplicates dispatch in React
2. **Replace resource surface with flat tools** — regresses agent tool-pick (~20 tool budget)
3. **HTTP proxy / serve-cockpit dev server** — PRD forbids

## New MCP App checklist

1. Register flat wrappers in `packages/mcp-server/src/index.ts`
2. Set `_meta.ui.visibility: ["app"]` on poll helpers
3. One entry tool with `resourceUri` for the agent to open the iframe
4. Iframe uses `callServerTool` + `extractToolText()` / `parseToolJson()` — not resource envelope
5. Run `npm run typecheck` on `src/views/<app>/` before push

**Reference implementation:** `packages/mcp-server/src/tools/eval_cockpit_wrappers.ts`, `context/changes/eval-cockpit-mcp-app/tool-bridge-adr.md`.

# NotDaybreak Watch skill-customization — DECIDED: Option 2

Source: Slack #wg-common-worker-layer thread C0BHGGA6PHC/p1784742716537469 (2026-07-23).
Endorsed by Garrett Spong, Yuliia (Reply 31), Ying Mao (Reply 32, closing action item).
Research artifact: elastic/project-daybreak#66. POC: spong/kibana#22 ([POC][do not merge]).

## Decision
Watch skill customization uses **Option 2**: a Watch-level skill **allowlist** passed as a
parameter into each `ai.agent` step (Orchestrator AND Workers), NOT a custom agent per Watch (Option 1, rejected).

## Mechanism (exact)
- Allowlist is **Watch-level config** — one place to manage, not per-agent.
- For each Agent instantiated by an `ai.agent` step: **effective skills = allowlist ∩ skills-already-exposed-to-that-agent** (INTERSECTION).
- A skill on the allowlist but never exposed to the agent → silently ignored.
- Safe-by-construction: the allowlist can only ever NARROW, never WIDEN an agent's skills.
- Worked example (Yuliia): allowlist [threat-intel, host-context, dark-web]
  - Agent A exposed [threat-intel, virustotal, otx] → ∩ = [threat-intel]
  - Agent B exposed [host-context, asset-db] → ∩ = [host-context]
  - dark-web never exposed anywhere → ignored.

## Platform enabler
Ying's PR (announced Reply 32, "by tomorrow") lets the `ai.agent` step accept skill overrides
(`configuration_overrides`: skill_ids + optionally instructions + tools). POC spong/kibana#22
lands as a FOLLOW-UP after `pnd` merges to main (separate AB-code review after hardening).

## Deferred (product, not technical blocker)
"Disable vs remove" toggle UX semantics — side effects when a shared skill is disabled.
Deferred to a product sync with Yuliia/James. UX leaning: capability(Worker)-level toggles primary,
skill toggles secondary with "disabling this degrades/disables Worker X" warnings.

## Related reframing
Orchestrator "no domain work" = maturity TARGET for mature Watches, not an authoring-time rule.
Workers are extracted when reuse/complexity/independent-testability appears; an orchestrator
`ai.agent` routing/policy step is explicitly allowed.

## Spike impact (deep-watch-mustard-integration)
Worker YAMLs at src/platform/packages/shared/kbn-workflows/managed/definitions/pnd/*.yaml
reference skills via prose `skill://…` mention only — no allowlist binding yet. Once Ying's
`ai.agent`-step override PR lands, add `configuration_overrides.skill_ids` (the Watch-level
allowlist) to each worker+orchestrator `ai.agent` step. Interim prose mention is functional
but NOT a hard allowlist.

# NotDaybreak / Kibana Workflow Engine — Conditional Dispatch & Templating Gotchas

Hard-won from live-verifying the Detection Watch orchestrator (`system-security-watch-detection`)
against the real workflow engine (deep-watch-mustard-integration worktree, :5580).

## 1. `if:` on a `workflow.execute`→worker step SILENTLY SKIPS the child
A bare step-level `if:` field wrapping a `type: workflow.execute` that targets a **worker**
workflow compiles to an `if_<name>` guard whose child never dispatches — the step reports
`completed` with `output: {}` and NO child execution runs (proven: `if: 'true'` still skipped;
removing `if:` made it run). Floor→Dark escalate works because it targets an **orchestrator**,
not because `if:`+workflow.execute is fine.
FIX: use an explicit `type: if` block with `condition:` + nested `steps:` (the compiler path
`createIfGraph` that alert_analysis_workflow.yaml uses). Nest run+emit steps inside it.

## 2. Condition syntax: use KQL existence `field:*`, NOT Liquid `${{ }}`
- `${{ expr }}` in a `condition:` does NOT reliably coerce to boolean. The `$` is emitted as a
  LITERAL char in console rendering (`${{ x }}` → `$<value>`), and a bare rendered string is not
  coerced to `true` by the condition evaluator → route silently skips even when the value is present.
- `${{ x != '' }}` is ALSO wrong: when the parent object is ABSENT, Liquid `nil != ''` → **true**,
  so the route WRONGLY runs (breaks mutual exclusivity between routes).
- CORRECT: bare KQL existence form `condition: 'event.ruleTuningTrigger.investigationId:*'`
  (matches alert_analysis line 1072 `"not steps...classification:*"`). Present→run, absent→skip.
  Pick a leaf that's ALWAYS present on a real payload and NEVER boolean-like.

## 3. Two templating syntaxes (alert_analysis line 176 comment)
`${{ }}` preserves booleans/numbers; `{{ }}` renders strings. In `kibana.request` bodies,
object/number fields passed between steps MUST use quoted `'${{ steps.X.output.field }}'` or they
stringify → downstream Zod `.parse()` throws (`expected object/number, received string` → HTTP 400).

## 4. Run inputs land under `event.*`, not `inputs.*`
`POST /api/workflows/workflow/{id}/run` body `{inputs:{event:{...}}}` → orchestrator reads
`{{ event.<field> }}`. Referencing `inputs.<field>` yields nothing (silent skip).

## 5. Managed workflow registration
A new managed workflow must be added to BOTH `PND_WATCH_WORKFLOW_IDS` (install loop) AND
`managedWorkflowDefinitions` in `managed/definitions/index.ts` (the id→definition registry the
client resolves against) or installStatic throws "Unknown managed workflow id".

## 6. Divergent enums bite silently
Adding a new watch tier (`watch-detection`, `watch-ad`) to `sourceWatchSchema` is not enough —
`workerEvaluationRecordSchema.watch` is a SEPARATE hardcoded enum; emit route's `.parse()` throws
HTTP 500 if the tier is missing there. Grep every `z.enum([...watch...])` when adding a tier.

## Run/verify contract
- Run: `POST /api/workflows/workflow/{id}/run` `{inputs:{event:{...}}}` (Api-Version 2023-10-31)
- Poll: `GET /api/workflows/executions/{id}?includeOutput=true` — terminal: completed/failed/error/timed_out
- `workflow.execute`→worker children run ASYNC; poll can show `waiting_for_child`. Verify via
  observable side-effect (proposal count delta in `pnd-canonical-proposals`), not just parent status.
- Server TS / package definition changes need a full Kibana restart (`--no-watch` does NOT hot-reload).

## 7. `ai.agent` structured output: use `with.schema:` (JSON-schema), NOT `structured_output:`
A flat `structured_output: {key: type}` map on an `ai.agent` step is SILENTLY IGNORED — the step
returns free text and `steps.X.output.structured_output` is `null` (fields fall through to
`| default:`). The working form (alert_analysis, floor/dark/deep workers) is a full JSON-schema:
```
with:
  message: >...
  schema:
    type: object
    properties: { field: { type: string, enum: [...], description: ... } }
    required: [field, ...]
```
Then read `steps.X.output.structured_output.<field>`. Grep new workers for `structured_output:` —
it's the wrong form.

# Operator Execution Style

Pairs with `feedback_proactive_operator_execution.md` (the core "run commands yourself,
don't hand off shell recipes" rule). Additional standing conventions:

- **Always provision a full working env** (connectors, Fleet, license, demo script) so the
  operator never has to assemble pieces themselves.
- **Maintain scripted, reusable demo-env recipes** — leverage `security-data-generator-app`,
  `local.propose-demo-env`, and for cloud PR demos: `ci:cloud-deploy` +
  `ci:cloud-persist-deployment` labels for persistent Cloud QA + a GCP Defend VM enrolled to
  the deployment. Don't one-off reinvent per skill/PM demo.
- **Endpoint response-actions demos** (isolate/release/scan/processes) require a **live
  enrolled Defend host** — synthetic endpoint fixtures alone are insufficient, unlike
  forensics read-only analysis which can run against fixtures.
- Run local Kibana demo/dev stacks with **`--no-base-path`**.
- When the operator says they don't know skills/evals, **don't defer decisions** — follow
  plugin best practices (`system.guide`, EDD journey) autonomously.
- When asked to fix and ship, drive through validate → commit → PR → merge on green CI
  without stopping at a plan unless genuinely blocked.
- **Never send Slack messages** unless explicitly asked (draft-only is fine).
- For local daemons (treadmill, MCP), rebuild/restart and probe live endpoints before
  declaring done; smoke end-to-end before skill/eval work.
- Deep analysis and tooling audits ship as **standalone HTML artifacts** (dark mode
  preferred).
- **Security LLM matrix HTML for PM/management handoff** must include per-cell score
  provenance (source build/run, golden-cluster trace/eval links) plus an explicit
  improvement backlog — not raw numbers alone.
- **Team-shareable planning/alignment boards** = self-contained HTML with build-time
  markdown embed (`npm run build:board` pattern), **not Cursor Canvas** (Canvas is
  in-session only — see `feedback_shareable_html_planning_board.md`).

## Benchmarker/eval infra operational conventions

- Start EDOT before the first converse/eval and restart EDOT after Scout/ES crashes so
  OTLP lands in `traces-*`.
- **`elastic-llm-benchmarker` on serverless still needs EDOT + SSH tunnels** for vLLM
  Prometheus/OTLP from the GPU VM — validate `metrics-*`/`traces-*` after deploy, not just
  the benchmark-results indices.
- **Benchmarker model queue:** deprioritize 8B, **24B+ floor**, rotate Mistral/European
  models alongside Qwen/Ornith, always latest release per family.
- **Don't open/prepare an EDOT PR** unless explicitly requested.
- **Wait for complete CI/eval/babysit results** before iterating on partial output.
- Reproduce and fix root cause on the branch (feature flags, wiring, setup gaps) before
  filing upstream Kibana bugs.
- Security LLM matrix: **prefer local Scout iteration** via
  `scripts/run-local-matrix-suite.sh` (unit→smoke→run-fast→run on Scout+EDOT) over
  sequential on-demand CI wall-clock.

## Shared-package change discipline

- **Never modify the shared `@kbn/evals` package directly** to fix a single suite's
  evaluator/system-prompt — copy the original logic into that suite and change it there,
  or land a properly-validated shared-scorer change (see
  `feedback_kbn_evals_evaluator_placement_pattern.md`).
- New evaluators for a specific domain (e.g. security) should live outside the main
  `kbn-evals` package — check for an existing `kbn-evals-extensions`-style sibling package
  or shared/common pattern before adding to core.

name: reference_security_matrix_batch_runner_resilience
description: run-security-evals-batch.sh resilience fixes on kibana-i9 — port cross-wiring, memory gate, work-stealing, liveness recovery, Playwright workers default
type: reference

# Security matrix batch runner resilience (`run-security-evals-batch.sh`)

Repo: `agent-builder-skill-dev-cursor-plugin` (`scripts/run-security-evals-batch.sh`). Kibana framework pieces land on `fix/weekly-evals-matrix` (PR [elastic/kibana#274606](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/274606)).

## Port cross-wiring (distinct from memory-pressure failures)

**Symptom:** worker-0 suite logs show `fetch failed` against **worker-1's ports** (`localhost:15002` ES / `15003` Kibana) while worker-0's own stack is on `15000`/`15001`.

**Root cause:** `SCOUT_SERVERS_ROOT` resolves to `<REPO_ROOT>/.scout/servers` with a **single** `local.json`. Parallel batch workers overwrite the same file; Playwright loads the last writer's ports.

**Fix (two layers):**
1. **Batch script:** export `CI_PARALLEL_PROCESS_NUMBER=<worker_id>` in each worker's tmux boot/suite shell so Scout port math stays worker-local (commit `5988bd4` class).
2. **Kibana framework:** worker-specific Scout config path in `kbn-scout-info/src/paths.ts` (commit `a4a8c70a2be4` on `fix/weekly-evals-matrix`).

Do not attribute cross-wired ports to Stage 2 memory exhaustion — check which `localhost:15xxx` port failed first.

## Memory / host pressure

| Check | When | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `check_memory_pressure` | Batch start (`BATCH_MIN_FREE_MEM_PCT`, default 15%) | Complements existing `check_disk_pressure` (10% free disk) |
| Stop `com.i9.edd-kibana` + `com.i9.edd-runner` | Before/during Stage 2 on `kibana-i9` | Already in `~/AGENTS.md` — host swap exhaustion masquerades as "0 spans traced" |
| `BOOT_POLL_ATTEMPTS=1800` | Cold ES snapshot re-download (~620MB) | Default poll window too short after nightly cache invalidation |

## Orchestration resilience (skill-dev plugin commits)

- **`ensure_stack_alive`:** re-check Kibana+ES ports before each suite dispatch; reboot if stack died mid-run.
- **`wait_for_connectors_registered`:** after pass-2/2 boot, poll until preconfigured connectors are visible (avoids racing suite start).
- **EIS re-provision after ES wipe:** `findConnectorById` alias fallback needs live ES `/_inference` endpoints — re-run connector provisioning when ES data dir is fresh.
- **Per-worker boot isolation:** old behavior `exit 1` when *any* worker boot failed killed successful workers; now continue dispatch for workers that booted.
- **Work-stealing queue:** atomic `mv`-based suite claim lets idle workers pull from a shared queue (verified 5 workers / 50 suites, no dupes).
- **`((++i))` not `((i++))`:** under `set -e`, post-increment on queue enqueue evaluates to 0 and silently kills **every single-suite run** at "Finding ports".
- **`suite_workers()` default `--workers 2`:** multi-spec suites (`security-ai-rules`, `security-alert-triage`, `security-automatic-migrations`, `entity-analytics-v2`, `agent-builder`) get two Playwright workers on the same stack; single-spec suites stay at 1. Requires Kibana `kbn-evals --workers` plumbing (commit `02a1f2b92e47`).

## Operational gotchas

- **Reconcile `kibana-i9` drift:** resilience fixes were developed on the remote host first — compare `git diff scripts/run-security-evals-batch.sh` on i9 vs local before declaring converged.
- **tmux kill orphans ES JVM:** killing a tmux session stops Kibana/scout but Elasticsearch JVM may survive (~2.5GB) — `kill` orphaned `org.elasticsearch.bootstrap.Elasticsearch` after teardown.
- **Manual overflow dispatch is redundant** once work-stealing is deployed — duplicate suite runs waste RAM and produce misleading failures (Fleet package races on overflow stacks).
- **`gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` evaluator errors:** soft `label: error` scores in trace evaluators, not Playwright failures — pre-existing mapping gap when spans omit that field.

## Smoke validation discipline

User preference (Jul 12 2026): pick the **smallest suite** that exercises the changed path — e.g. `security-alert-triage` (2 specs) or `security-ai-rules` (2 specs) with `BATCH_WORKERS=1`, not `agent-builder` (30 specs) or full `evals_security_all`. Use `--dry-run` to validate CLI plumbing before booting Scout.

# Security LLM Matrix — On-Demand Eval Chain

# Security OSS / Self-Hosted LLM Matrix — Demand Map & Validated Models

Recurring, revenue-attached demand (Slack-sourced, 2024–2026) for Elastic to
recommend/support **open-source, self-hosted LLMs for Security**. The published
Security matrix regressed from several OSS models (v8.19) to **one** in v9+
(GPT-OSS-120B, rated ~3.5/10 "not recommended"), while **Observability recommends
many more** and has a far more mature OSS eval process. The real knowledge lives
in SDH comments + DMs + a stale Google Sheet, not the published docs.

## Validated eval results (internal, NOT yet published) — the highest-value asset
Patryk's own Agent-Builder/Attack-Discovery eval run via OpenRouter (DM w/ Florian
Jacobs, 2026-04-22) — concrete numbers to promote into the matrix:
- **Kimi K2.6** and **DeepSeek V3.2** tied #1: Basic=1.00 / Rubric=0.83 / Ran=1.00
  over every 8-scenario run. **DeepSeek ~45% faster** (12-min vs Kimi 22-min) —
  throughput advantage.
- **GLM-5.1**: structurally capable (Basic=1 every scored scenario) but SLOW —
  caught by the 30-min Playwright test.timeout; 6 ECONNRESETs from long
  generations hitting HTTP boundaries even at 10-min timeouts.
- **gpt-oss-120b**: tool-emission reliability issues — passed smoke tests but
  broke on bundled-alert AD prompts with "No tool call found in LLM response"
  (generated text instead of a tool call, crashed mid-suite). Native function
  calling brittle for large AD prompts.
- **qwen3.6-plus**: non-evaluable on OpenRouter — HTTP 404 because OR's Qwen
  endpoints reject the `tool_choice` body param Kibana's chatComplete adapter
  sends with native function calling. Fix: connector-level override to strip
  `tool_choice` (downgrades AD to "auto"), or wait for a compliant OR endpoint.
- BSI (2026-06-04 follow-up) reported good on-prem AD results with **Kimi K2.6**.

Model shortlist reasoning (2026-04-21): Kimi K2 Thinking (INT4-QAT, capability
anchor, ~520GB+256K ctx fits 1600GB, `--tool-call-parser kimi_k2`); GLM-4.6 FP8
(agentic workhorse, 200K ctx, ~400GB); Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 FP8
(tool-calling specialist, BFCL-v3 70.9, 22B active → high concurrency).

## Internally validated self-hosted models (from sdh-security-team#1417 + Steph's SDH reply)
Promote these into the published matrix with hardware + vLLM params:
- **Qwen3-32B** — validated 2×40GB A100 via vLLM; `--enable-auto-tool-choice
  --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3` + yarn rope-scaling
  (factor 4.0) + `--max-model-len 30000` + anti-duplicate-tool-call system
  prompt. Go-to for limited hardware. No Kibana feature flags — native function
  calling on.
- **Qwen3.6-27B-Int4** — quantized option for smaller hardware
  (`--tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --enable-prefix-caching`).
- **Mistral Small 3.2 (2506)** / **Magistral** — 3.2 explicitly trained for tool
  calling (vanilla leaked `[TOOL_CALLS]…`). magistral-small-2509 needs
  model-specific config (top_p, temp **0.7** — but Security Assistant sends 0.2;

# Skill-dev plugin enforced author journey

The plugin already had phase skills but entry points still routed authors directly to
suite generation. The fix is an **enforced, vendor-neutral chain** so PMs/devs shape
*what* to evaluate before scaffolding `@kbn/evals`.

## Phase chain (in order)

1. `skill-discover` — extend / create / reject
2. `skill-shape-problem` — persona, constraints, anti-goals, measurable outcomes
3. `skill-plan-prd` — acceptance criteria + build plan
4. `skill-design-evals` — AC → evaluator matrix, cases, thresholds
5. `skill-pre-flight` — environment + routing prechecks
6. Skill authoring (implementation)

Do **not** skip to `eval-generation` or authoring until shape + requirements exist.

# Treadmill ship-feature — Admin Merge Fallback

`treadmill ship-feature` runs `gh pr merge --auto --squash` as its final step. On repos where auto-merge is not enabled at the GitHub repo level (`enablePullRequestAutoMerge: false`), this fails with:

```
GraphQL: Auto merge is not allowed for this repository (enablePullRequestAutoMerge)
```

The PR is created, pushed, and CI runs — only the merge step fails. This is **not a bug** in the workflow; it's a repo-level setting that requires `scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` to enable. Per `feedback_skill_dev_pr_admin_merge`, the established fallback is admin merge.

## Correct sequence

1. `treadmill ship-feature` — runs lint + typecheck + test, pushes branch, opens PR, attempts auto-merge (will fail at this step).
2. `gh pr checks <N> --watch --interval 30` — wait for CI to go green.
3. `gh pr merge <N> --admin --squash --delete-branch` — admin-merge once CI passes.
   - `--delete-branch` may fail with `fatal: 'main' is already used by worktree at <path>` if a worktree has main checked out. The merge itself succeeds; only local branch cleanup fails. Verify with `gh pr view <N> --json state,mergedAt`.
4. Pull the merged SHA into local main (stash any pre-existing dirty changes first).

## When auto-merge IS enabled

Auto-merge waits for green CI and merges automatically — no manual step. The `--admin` fallback is unnecessary.

## Diagnostic

Check whether auto-merge is enabled:

```bash
gh repo view --json mergeCommitAllowed,autoMergeAllowed -q '.autoMergeAllowed'
```

If `false`, either run `scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` to enable it, or use the admin-merge fallback above.

## Confirmed

2026-06-30 — PR #128 (`fix(memory): rank export by recency and budget cap per category`) auto-merge failed on `patryks-treadmill`; admin-merged after CI green; verified `state=MERGED`, `mergedAt` populated.

2026-07-10 — PR #159 (`feat/scope-mechanical-checks-and-boot-reconcile`) hit the same failure. User confirmed the root cause is structural, not a one-off setting: **`patryks-treadmill` is a private repo, and GitHub auto-merge requires branch protection rules that aren't available/configured on this private repo tier** — so `--admin --squash` after green CI is the standing fallback here, not a transient bug to keep re-diagnosing. User explicit instruction: "auto merge is not available for private repo, so don't ask me again."

# Treadmill `claude-code` → 9router wiring

## Why user settings alone are insufficient

`claude-cli.ts` builds headless invocations with `getHookSafeClaudeArgs()`, which passes `--setting-sources project,local` to avoid user-level stop hooks. This **also skips** `~/.claude/settings.json` env overrides such as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:20128`.

## Correct wiring

Set on the **daemon process** (not just interactive CLI):

- `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:20128` (or Tailscale tunnel URL)
- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<9router api key>`
- `AO_CLAUDE_MODEL=main` — use the 9router **combo name**, not `cc/claude-sonnet-5` (user correction Jul 12 2026)

Injection paths (in order of preference):

1. `launchctl setenv` before daemon restart (ephemeral until reboot)
2. Extend `treadmill install` plist conditional env list
3. `~/.treadmill/secrets.env` (sourced by `run-daemon.sh`) — agent tools may block direct edits; operator can append manually

## Model selection in orchestrator

`orchestrator-loop.ts` reads `process.env.AO_CLAUDE_MODEL` for the `claude-code` agent model override. Verified Jul 12 2026: `main` combo reaches 9router and completes a simple local assertion job (~42s wall, may route to a cascade member like `kimi-k2.7-code`).

## Gotchas

- `cc/claude-sonnet-5` may 429 or be unrecognized; `main` and `cheap` combo names work when passed directly to `claude --print`.
- Upstream Claude/Copilot rate limits (429) block verification even when routing is correct — distinguish plumbing vs quota.
- Secrets-bearing files (`secrets.env`) are hook-blocked for agent writes; use `launchctl setenv` or hand edits to the operator.

# Treadmill Command Center — Next-Action Execute

Shipped PRs [#87](https://github.com/patrykkopycinski/patryks-treadmill/pull/87)–[#91](https://github.com/patrykkopycinski/patryks-treadmill/pull/91) (Tier-1 from `docs/prd-proactive-work-intelligence.md`).

## HTTP surfaces

| Endpoint | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /api/next-actions?limit=N` | Ranked actions; each item includes `executable: boolean` |
| `POST /api/next-actions/:id/dismiss` | Permanent dismiss or snooze (`{ snoozeHours?, reason? }`) |
| `POST /api/next-actions/:id/execute` | One-click execution (reads from loop cache) |

Dashboard: **Do it** when `executable === true`. Browser title: `(N)` pending count; healing critical/warn prefixes win.

## Executable rules

| Rule | Action | Default auto-execute (`AO_AUTO_EXECUTE_NEXT_ACTIONS=1`) |
|------|--------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `jobFailedRetryable` | Job retry + task → ready | **Yes** |
| `planDraftStale` | Activate plan (`skipClarify: true`) | No (yes with `*`) |
| `planPausedLong` | Same activate path | No (yes with `*`) |
| `prChangesRequested` | `postPrReviewThreadsApply` (macroscope apply-feedback; may push) | No (yes with `*`) |

PR merge and promote remain manual.

## Auto-execute env gate

Set in `~/.treadmill/secrets.env`, reload via `treadmill install`:

```bash
AO_AUTO_EXECUTE_NEXT_ACTIONS=1          # retryable jobs only
# AO_AUTO_EXECUTE_NEXT_ACTIONS=*      # all executable rules above
# AO_AUTO_EXECUTE_NEXT_ACTIONS=jobFailedRetryable,planDraftStale
```

Loop: max **1** auto-execute per **60s**, highest urgency, after 30s next-actions compute.

## MCP (Cursor reload required after MCP package change)

| Tool | Profile | Purpose |
|------|---------|---------|
| `treadmill_next_actions` | core | List ranked actions |
| `treadmill_execute_next_action` | core | POST execute (`actionId` = `id` from list) |
| `treadmill_dismiss_action` | **core** + plan | Dismiss/snooze |

Non-executable execute → HTTP 400 `action is not auto-executable`.

## Background maintenance (#87–#91)

- **Session reconciler** — every 2 min; drains stuck `active` sessions
- **Ephemeral janitor** — hourly `sweepStaleEphemeralPlans()`; completes stale ephemeral plans, cancels old ephemeral failed jobs, cancels failed jobs on long-**completed** non-ephemeral plans (`terminalPlanJobsCancelled`)
- **Next-actions snapshot** — excludes ephemeral plan jobs; job-based rules only for plans in `active|paused|failed|draft`; `githubIssueUnlinked` capped at 10

## Key files

- `packages/orchestrator/src/next-action-executor.ts`
- `packages/orchestrator/src/session-reconciler.ts`
- `packages/orchestrator/src/ephemeral-plan-janitor.ts`
- `packages/orchestrator/src/next-actions-snapshot.ts`
- `packages/orchestrator/src/orchestrator-loop.ts`
- `packages/orchestrator/src/knowledge-memory-sync.ts` — import/export/sync (#91)
- `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` — `treadmill_execute_next_action`, `treadmill_dismiss_action` (core)

## Still open (Tier-1 roadmap)

- Opt-in auto-dispatch for `prChangesRequested` (execute exists; auto-execute needs `*` or explicit allowlist)
- `featureAllPlansCompleted` / promote as executable next-action
- Morning brief + Hermes digest wiring

# Treadmill constraint effectiveness gates

Treadmill auto-generates constraints from recurring gate failures (`gate_failures` / `constraints`
tables, `selfAudit()` maintenance, dispatch-time injection). Two **effectiveness gates** keep the
constraint/pattern set from accumulating dead weight:

- **`constraints.baseline_count` expiry** — a constraint records a baseline failure count for its
  failure class; a constraint that never reduces that class's failure rate is **expired** rather than
  re-injected forever. Ineffective constraints self-prune.
- **Outcome-correlated pattern recall** — `session_patterns.success_recalls` /
  `session_patterns.failure_recalls`, combined with `jobs.recalled_pattern_ids`, gate pattern recall
  to **outcome-correlated** patterns, not merely frequently-seen ones. A pattern that correlates with
  failures when recalled is down-weighted; frequency alone does not earn recall.

**Why:** naive constraint auto-generation and frequency-based recall both drift toward noise — stale
constraints get re-injected and high-frequency-but-useless patterns dominate recall. Gating on
measured effectiveness (did it reduce the failure class? did recall correlate with success?) keeps the
self-improvement loop signal-positive.

**Where:** treadmill orchestrator (`packages/orchestrator/src/`), self-audit maintenance path.
Related: pass convergence at `/api/plan/:id/convergence`.

# Treadmill Daemon — Misc Operational Facts

## `treadmill_capture_idea` MCP tool 400 error

Returns `HTTP 400: body required` on any payload — a known field-name mismatch between the
MCP tool wrapper (`title`/`description`) and the server route (expects `body`). The fix
landed in source, but killing/respawning the MCP server process out-of-band from Cursor's
own lifecycle management breaks the stdio connection (`serverStatus: error`). **Reload via
Cursor's MCP UI, not a manual `kill`.**

## launchd log rotation

launchd does **not** rotate `StandardOutPath`/`StandardErrorPath` — logs grow unbounded.
`scripts/run-daemon.sh` does a boot-time tail-truncate when the daemon log exceeds ~50 MB
(keeps the last ~5 MB). This runs once per boot and is effective because launchd respawns
the daemon on crash-restart cycles anyway. Reinstall via `treadmill install` whenever the
wrapper script changes (it gets copied to `~/.treadmill/bin/run-daemon.sh` at install time).

## `ProcessType` for latency-sensitive LaunchAgents

Use **`ProcessType=Standard`** (not `Background`) for latency-sensitive LaunchAgents (Node
dashboards/API servers) — `Background` QoS throttles CPU/IO and can stretch a sub-second
startup to minutes before the port binds.

# Treadmill ES Intelligence — Boot & Backfill Reference

## Boot sequence (when `TREADMILL_ES_ENABLED=1`)

Deferred off critical path (post-`setImmediate` as of 2026-06):

1. `runWarmUpQuery()`
2. `provisionIndices()`
3. `scheduleReconciliation(db)`
4. `backfillIssuesToEs(db)` — skips if `treadmill-issues` already has docs
5. `runBackfillIfNeeded(db, dataDir)` — fire-and-forget
6. `scanProjectSkills(daemonSourceRepo)` + `indexProjectSkills` — background

Dual-writes before indices exist degrade gracefully (logged, non-fatal).

## Backfill policy

```typescript
// shouldRunFullBackfill(esCount, sqliteCount)
// true only when sqliteCount > 0 && esCount === 0
// Partial drift (esCount > 0 && esCount < sqliteCount) → skip; dual-write + reconciliation cover gaps
```

Per-index `await flushNow()` after full backfill batch; paced by `TREADMILL_ES_BACKFILL_PACE_EVERY` (default 500).

## Logs to grep

| Log prefix | Meaning |
|------------|---------|
| `[es-backfill] partial (...)` | Skipping re-backfill — expected after fix |
| `[es-backfill] enqueued N tasks` | Full backfill running — should only happen on empty index |
| `[es-issue-indexer] ... skipping backfill` | Issues index populated |
| `[project-skills] indexed N skills from` | Background scan complete |

## Reconciliation drift (informational)

Common on long-running installs: plans/jobs/tasks counts differ between ES and SQLite. Not a boot blocker once partial re-backfill is disabled.

## Key paths

- `packages/orchestrator/src/es-backfill.ts` — `shouldRunFullBackfill`, `runBackfillIfNeeded`
- `packages/orchestrator/src/index.ts` — ES boot `setImmediate` block (~line 707)
- `packages/orchestrator/src/project-skill-scanner.ts` — full-tree walk; expensive on kibana
- Daemon logs: `~/Library/Logs/patryks-treadmill/ao-orchestrator.{stdout,stderr}.log`
- Live DB: `packages/orchestrator/.ao-verifier/verifier.db` (launchd cwd = orchestrator pkg)

# Treadmill health endpoints and CLI probes

## Two health routes

| Route | Purpose | DB / blocking |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/health/lite` | Liveness — watchdog probe, boot polling | None (`uptime` + `pid` only) |
| `GET /api/health` | Readiness — plans/jobs/fleet/scanners snapshot | Sync SQLite (`safeCount`, `listPlansLite`, profile queries) |

Under heavy DB contention (boot warm-up, knowledge import, WAL checkpoint), inline
`/api/health` work on the main thread can exceed CLI timeouts and throw
`DaemonUnreachableError` even when the daemon is fine.

## Full health caching (shipped)

`getHealth()` serves a **30s cached snapshot** with fresh `uptime`/`memory`. When stale,
it kicks a **single background refresh** — never blocks the request path on SQLite.

Watchdog already probes `/api/health/lite` (main.ts). CLI liveness checks should prefer
lite during boot/warm-up (allow 60–90s).

## CLI resilience

`daemonRetry()` in `packages/cli/src/daemon-client.ts` retries **only** on
`DaemonUnreachableError` (bounded backoff; default `retries=0` elsewhere). Wired into
shared memory-command helpers (`memory-import-knowledge`, export, stats) — not `run`/`stop`/`doctor`.

## Restart and false negatives

- **`treadmill stop`** can emit **"No daemon is running"** during an event-loop stall while
  the process is alive — HTTP to stop times out like any other CLI call.
- **Verify alive:** `curl /api/health/lite` → check `uptime` + `pid`.
- **Force restart (launchd):** `launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.patryks-treadmill`
  (see `feedback_launchd_hook_kickstart_vs_bootstrap.md` — bootstrap/load may be hook-blocked).

When the loop is genuinely wedged (lite also times out 10–20s), diagnose with
`sample <pid> 4 -mayDie` — sync `better-sqlite3` or `spawnSync` on the main thread.

# Treadmill MCP Tool Exposure & Testing

`packages/mcp/src/index.ts` serves the `user-patryks-treadmill` Cursor MCP server (typically `--profile=core`).

## Registration ≠ exposure

A tool registered with `server.tool(...)` is **not callable** until it appears in `PROFILES[<profile>]` for the active profile. Case study: `treadmill_recall` was registered but absent from `PROFILES.core` — agents on `--profile=core` could not call it until added next to `treadmill_semantic_search` (commit `47321b1`).

## Verify with tools/list smoke

```bash
cd packages/mcp
printf '%s\n%s\n' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"smoke","version":"0"}}}' \
  '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' \
  | node dist/index.js --profile=core 2>/dev/null
```

Confirm the tool name is in the `tools/list` result — not just in source registration.

## Cursor descriptor cache

Cursor materializes MCP tool descriptors under `.cursor/projects/<slug>/mcps/<server>/tools/*.json` from the server's `tools/list`. This cache can lag behind an MCP reload — **missing descriptor file is not proof the tool is unregistered**. Prefer direct `tools/list` smoke over globbing the descriptor folder.

## Unit-testing self-executing modules

`index.ts` boots the MCP server on import (self-executing). **Do not import it in-process for unit tests.** Pattern:

1. Extract pure logic to a sibling module (e.g. `http-retry.ts`: `isTransientCallError`, `isUnreachable`, `UNREACHABLE_CODES`).
2. Unit-test the sibling directly (`node --import tsx --test src/http-retry.test.ts`).
3. Keep integration/registration tests as subprocess spawns of `dist/index.js` (existing `index.test.ts` pattern).

## Discovery seam for gated deferrals

When an optional "if X recurs" item has no recurrence data, ship a **discovery seam** this cycle — make the currently-silent path observable (e.g. stderr log on each transient MCP retry: `[treadmill-mcp] transient failure on <path> ...`) — rather than a speculative profiling pass. The log line becomes the gate for deeper investigation (`address-known-limitations` discovery-seam tier).

**Confirmed:** Session d4c1da5e (Jul 5 2026): http-retry extraction `031e54a`, retry-log seam `da1fabd`, `treadmill_recall` in core `47321b1`.
